   stands worn. The initial surface z₀ is the isostatic rest height of step 2 plus the row's `heightM` where the
   profile's shape is 1 (never U integrated over the age, which would stand tens of kilometres high).
6. **Fluvial erosion by the steady-state fixed point; hillslope relaxation** (J-V13.108). The stream-power law ∂z/∂t
   = U − K A^m S^n (m = `erosion.m`, n = 1, K by bedrock class) is solved at its steady state, not stepped: along each
   flow path the slope obeys S = (U/K) A^(−m) (Flint's law), so z is one integral from the outlet upstream, z_i = z_r +
   Δx_ir (U_i/K_i) A_i^(−m). Because the drainage tree depends on z, the op iterates `erosion.iterations` times — build
   the tree (the lifted priority flood with lakes kept as flats at their spill height, the two-gradient flats, D8 in the
   fixed neighbour order, V13 §3.5.1), order it as a **stack** (an O(N) depth-first ordering from each base-level node
   so every node follows its receiver — the one new routine beside the lifted core), accumulate A (one reverse walk;
   **precipitation-weighted** when `erosion.precipWeighted`: a single annual wind march of V13 §3.4 (6) run once over
   z₀ at the formation grid gives the weights, so the wet flank of a range erodes faster — the only climate read inside
   formation, never the monthly march), integrate z up the stack — and converges in 5–15 iterations because the tree
   changes only at divides (a fully dendritic relief obeying the Hack and bifurcation statistics, T-V13-58). After the
   fixed point each boundary's relief is scaled about its base level so its crest lies in its row's `heightM` band (the
   shape and the Hack statistics unchanged): at the table's K and U the steady relief of a 50–200 km catchment would
   otherwise stand 5–39 km, an impossible height, and the band is what the scenario promises; the mean land height is
   reported against 500–1 200 m (T-V13-58). Then the
   **talus relaxation**: `erosion.talusPasses` eight-neighbour passes that move material from a cell to its lower
   neighbours where the slope exceeds `talusDegByBedrock` (at the grid's cell hillslope diffusion is sub-grid; the
   talus is the term that matters). The transient run of hundreds of steps is never taken: at the formation grid it
   would cost 1.5–14 s, over budget above the province rung, and the fixed point gives the same steady relief.
7. **Glacial carving and the sea-level stands.** (a) The glacial-maximum equilibrium-line surface from latitude
   (`glacial.elaByLatDeg`, interpolated), the palaeo-offset `lgmOffsetDeciC` and the annual precipitation (a wet flank
   lower by up to `elaWetDepressionM`), scaled by the knob `iceExtent`; the **ice mask** = the cells above the line
   plus every downstream cell reached by ice flux (Σ accumulation above the line along the stack until ablation below
   it exhausts it: one stack pass); the **carve** along glaciated thalwegs lowers the bed ∝ flux^(l/2) (l =
   `erosionExponent`) and widens the cross-section to a parabola whose width ∝ flux^`troughWidthExponent`,
   overdeepening allowed (no monotone-bed constraint: the bed may rise toward the snout), a cirque bowl cut at each
   glacier head on the polar-facing slope; W2's lakes-by-spill-height later makes every overdeepening a **glacial
   lake** — formation never fills them. (b) The sea-level history: a bounded transient — `seaLevel.lowstandSteps` (10) implicit steps of `lowstandYr` ÷ 10
   (20 000 years in all) with U = 0 and the base level at `seaLevel.glacialLowM`, over the cells within `riaBandKm` of
   the lowstand coast (a steady state has no span, and a lowered base level alone would drop the whole land by the
   stand; O(N) per step, ≈ 0.2 s at the realm rung inside `formationMs`) — cuts the valleys across the exposed shelf
   for the last stand, then the datum is set to 0 (V13 §2.1):
   every valley segment now below 0 within `riaBandKm` of the coast is a **ria**, every glacial trough reaching the
   coast a **fjord** with its sill at the former snout; the rebound field `reboundShare` × the former ice's thickness — read as `reboundMaxM` (300) under the ice mask,
   since no thickness is computed — × (1 − e^(−t/`reboundTauYr`)) minus the eustatic rise, where positive, names **raised beaches** at the deglaciation's
   shoreline. `seaLevel.stands` > 1 repeats (b) per stand at decreasing lows.
8. **Bedrock.** Per formation cell by the boundary class and the profile that made it: arc volcanics along an arc,
   a folded belt in a collision range, shield on an old continental interior, flood basalt in a rift, limestone and
   evaporite in a shallow basin (a foreland or a closed rift basin below the datum at its stand), alluvium on a
   floodplain (a cell within one formation cell of a channel whose A exceeds `channelInitCells` × 50 and whose slope is
   under 0.5 %), till under the ice mask, ash within `deposits.ashRadiusKm` of a volcano, young lava on a hotspot's
   edifice, ordinary sedimentary elsewhere → `WorldRaster.bedrock`; `geology` is derived by `bedrockToGeology` (the
   four classes W4's permeability and W5's resource rules keep reading).
9. **Soils.** The soil-forming factors per formation cell — the formation-time annual climate of step 6 (MAT, MAP,
   the aridity index MAP ÷ PET with PET by V13 §3.4 (7)'s law), the slope, the wetland flag (A over
   `wetlandAccumCells` ÷ `formationRatio`² on a flat), the groundwater depth (a first table by V13 §3.5.4's rule at the
   formation grid), the permafrost flag, the parent class (step 8) and the surface age (`surfaceAgeByLandform`: zero on
   fresh lava and an active floodplain, the deglaciation's age on till, the orogeny's `ageMyr` elsewhere, the shield's
   10⁸ yr) — through `world.soil`'s first-match list (V13 §2.3's twelve rows) → `WorldRaster.soil`, with `surfaceAge`
   kept for a later `weather` op. The **fine-scale overrides** are applied by every reader at read time, never stored
   (a fine cell whose slope exceeds 30 % reads `entisol`; one on an active floodplain reads alluvial `entisol`), so
   soil costs one formation-grid byte per cell.
10. **The landforms, the bake and the deletion.** The op traces its landforms as outlines on the formation grid, each a
   `Landform` entity (V13 §2.2) with its `formed` provenance in words: a **range** (the connected cells above a crest
   threshold along a convergent boundary; its crest the ridge line), a **volcano** or **caldera** (an arc or hotspot
   edifice; a collapsed one), a **rift**, a **fault** (a transform), a **hotspot chain**, each **glacial lake**,
   **fjord** and **cirque**, a **plateau**, a **basin**, a **trench**, an **arc**, each **ria**, a **raised beach**, a
   **suture**, an **escarpment** (a rift shoulder's edge); each named by W9 (V13 §3.10). Then the **bake**: the op's
   `baked` is written — the formation-grid DEM as content-hashed `fields` chunks, `bedrock`, `soil`, `surfaceAge`, the
   landform ids, `formation.version` and the stats (the land share, the Hack exponent and the bifurcation ratio of the
   relief, T-V13-58) — and the block set, the velocities, the boundaries, the distance fields, the stack, the ice mask
   and every intermediate are **deleted**: none exists in any digest (T-V13-57), none is ever read again, no crust block
   moves after this line. W1 then continues with the ops after it over the fine grid, the baked DEM upsampled
   bilinearly as the working raster's start.
11. **The `weather` op** (the physics pass's `weather` depth, V13 §4.1). Over the ground as it stands at the op's
   position in the recipe, downsampled to the formation grid over the scope: ⌈`years` ÷ 10⁵⌉ implicit steps (at most
   ten) of the stream-power law with U = 0 — the stack update z_i = (z_i + F_i z_r) ÷ (1 + F_i), F_i = K Δt A_i^m ÷
   Δx_ir, receivers first, unconditionally stable for n = 1, where an explicit step is stable only below Δt ≈ Δx ÷
   (K A^m), about 1 300 years on an alluvial trunk —, `years` of hillslope diffusion (D × years, explicit, its length scale under one cell at campaign spans),
   the talus relaxation, the soil re-aged by `years` through the soil law (an old field's `entisol` becomes
   `inceptisol`, an `alfisol` at 10⁴ years), a lake silted where its inflow carries sediment for the span; the delta,
   the soil and any new landform (a new ria after a sea-level `setSurface`; a filled glacial lake) baked as the op's
   payload; the span's effect computed from E = K A^m S over the scope and stated to the DM before the commit ("over
   10 000 years the valley floors of this shield lower by about 1 m; the soils age one class").

*Determinism:* every draw on `world.formation`; the flood and the stack in row-major order with cell-index ties; the
fixed point's iterations fixed in count; every float through `dmath` — byte-identical at generation across platforms
(T-V13-58) and never re-run thereafter (T-V13-57). *Budget:* `formationMs` (V13 §6: ≈ 0.27 / 1.0 / 2.3 s on the
formation grid; the memory 32 B per formation cell ≈ 18 MB at the continent rung, freed at the bake). *Edges:* a
scenario at a rung it does not admit is refused at W0 (`refuse.world.scenarioRung`); `blocks` 0 at the continent rung
reads the regional context; a world whose requirements lock it to no sea with an island-arc scenario is refused at W0
(`refuse.world.requirements`); a relict belt that the erosion of step 6 wears below 200 m is kept as a `suture`
landform with no range label and reported `W_FORMATION_RELICT`; an orogeny older than 1 000 Myr reads as `shield`.

### 3.3 W2 Features and surfaces

1. **Flood fill.** Cells with `dem` < 0 are water, else land; connected water components by 4-neighbour flood fill in
   canonical cell order; a water component that touches the extent's border is an **ocean** feature, any other a **lake**
   candidate; a land component is a **landmass** (its id by its lowest-then-leftmost cell), the index W7 and W8 read.
2. **Lakes by spill height.** W2 runs the priority flood (the lifted core, §2.3's mechanism) over the fine dem with the
   ocean cells as the queue's seeds and the border cells at their own height: a depression whose fill depth (spill height
   − floor) ≥ `lakeMinDepthCm` becomes a **lake** feature whose cells are those filled, with a `WaterSurface` of kind
   `lake` at the spill height (`elevationCm`); a saddle within `breachToleranceCm` of the sea surface is **breached**: the
   depression joins the ocean feature, its cells read water at 0, reported `W_WORLD_LAKE_BREACHED`. A water component of
   step 1 that lies in no filled depression (a sunken plain the recipe dug below 0 but which drains to the border) is an
   ocean arm. The sea's `WaterSurface` is one record at 0 cm (`kind: 'sea'`, `tidalRangeCm` from `world.hydro`'s cell, V13
   §2.3), `cause: 'generation'`. The coast polylines (`coast`, V13 §2.2's companion record) are the marching-squares
   outline of each landmass's water boundary in world cm, one ring set per landmass, the view's and the charter's source.
3. **Open or closed, subtype.** After W3's climate and W4's accumulation (W2 writes the records; W4 fills these two
   fields in its lake step, V13 §3.5.2): a lake is `open` when its inflow (the accumulated runoff into its cells, W4)
   exceeds its evaporation (its area × `evapMm`); an open lake has its outlet reach at the spill cell; a lake's `subtype`
   is, by one precedence at both scales (the frame's V13 §3.12.1 reads this rule): `fresh` when open; `dry` (drawn as a
   flat) when closed and its evaporation ≥ 4 × its inflow; `salt` when closed and its climate arid (precipitation <
   evaporation); else `brackish`; its `iceWeeks` are the weeks whose temperature by the seasonal curve (V13 §3.4 (4))
   lies below −3 °C — ice is a season, never a subtype. The rules' shape is the reference's (`fmg-physical-pipeline.md` §3.14 as
   evidence); the thresholds are ours.
4. **The coast outline.** The ocean feature's boundary, traced as rings along cell edges and simplified by
   Visvalingam at 0.5 × the fine cell, is the world's coast polyline set (`WorldRaster`'s companion record
   `coast: WorldPointCm[][]`, in the entities block), the view's and the exports' line and P1's coast-side test input.
   Coastline fractalisation is a view-time displacement (V13 §5.1), never geometry (J-V13.8).

*Output:* the features, the sea and lake surfaces, the coast outline. The reason record of each lake names its spill
cell, fill depth and threshold.

### 3.4 W3 Climate

On the coarse raster; every value integer (deci-°C, mm/yr, cdeg), every transcendental through `dmath` (§6.5).

1. **Latitude.** Row r's latitude is `latBox.south + (latBox.north − south) × (r + 0.5) ÷ rows` (an equirectangular
   box; the only use of degrees).
1b. **The order (one fixed pass, no iteration; V13 §3.17's determinism):** (i) a first temperature with
   `continentality` by the distance rule (`continentalityReachKm`) and no coastal anomaly; (ii) the winds of every
   month from (i) (step 5); (iii) the currents and `sstAnomalyDeciC` from (ii) (step 6b); (iv) the twelve marches with
   the maritime fraction (steps 3, 6); (v) the final temperature from `maritime` and (iii) (step 2), the fitted curve
   (step 4) and the evaporation (step 7) — the winds are never recomputed from (v), so two implementations agree byte
   for byte (T-V13-59).
2. **Temperature, per month** (J-V13.112): the annual mean at sea level T_sea(lat) as before — `equatorDeciC` for
   |lat| ≤ `tropicsDeg`, beyond it linear in |lat| to `poleDeciC` at 90° (the explicit pole input, item 138 (c)); the
   month's sea-level temperature T_sea,m = T_sea + A_sea × cos(2π (m − m_hot) ÷ 12), the sea-level amplitude A_sea =
   `seasonAmpMaxDeciC` × sin(|lat|) × ((1 − `seasonContinentalShare`) + `seasonContinentalShare` × (1 − `maritime`))
   (step 3) and m_hot the calendar hemisphere's hottest month (V13 §2.3's phase rows read in months); on land T_m =
   T_sea,m − `lapseDeciCPerKm` × (dem ÷ 1 000 m); on water T_m = T_sea,m + the month's `sstAnomalyDeciC` (step 6b: a
   warm current's coast reads warmer, a cold or upwelling coast colder, the anomaly fading inland over
   `currents.coastalReachKm` on land cells too). Stored `tempMonthDeciC[m]`; `tempDeciC` their mean.
3. **The maritime fraction** (continentality by upwind fetch; J-V13.112): the march of step 6 carries, beside its
   moisture, a maritime fraction that resets to 1 over water and relaxes toward 0 over land with the e-folding length
   `maritime.efoldKm` — so a cell 50 km inland on an east coast in the westerlies is continental and a cell 500 km
   inland on the west coast still a third maritime (e^(−500 ÷ 400) ≈ 0.29); `maritime` is the annual mean over the twelve monthly marches (the first
   month's march runs with the last month's winds as its start); `continentality` = 1 − `maritime`, the field every
   existing reader keeps. The former distance-to-ocean rule (`continentalityReachKm`) serves only the import's
   derive-only mode, where no march runs.
4. **The seasonal curve, fitted** (per cell: mean, amplitude, phase): the first harmonic of the twelve monthly
   temperatures — T their mean, A and the phase from the cosine and sine sums over the months (through `dmath`), the
   phase rounded to the week; on a cell with no coastal anomaly the fit returns `phaseWeekNorth` in the calendar
   hemisphere and `phaseWeekSouth` in the other within a week (the calendar hemisphere is the north unless
   `WorldRecipe.calendarSouth`; on a host-bound world it is the one the host's seasons name, V13 §2.3). The
   temperature at week w is T + A × cos(2π (w − phase) ÷ 52) — the formula every reader of a seasonal state uses (V13
   §3.12.4; the host's calendar reads `week` as §4.11's), unchanged; a reader that wants the month itself reads
   `tempMonthDeciC`. Stored `seasonAmpDeciC`, `seasonPhaseWeek`.
5. **Winds, per month** (J-V13.112). For each month m and each coarse column x the convergence zone's latitude is
   φ_I(x, m) = `belts.itczDeg` + A_I(x) × cos(2π (m − m_hot − `belts.lagMonths`) ÷ 12), A_I(x) between
   `itczSwingOceanDeg` and `itczSwingLandDeg` by the column's land fraction within `belts.landFetchKm` of the zone
   (the land fraction beyond the map's edge is the world context's — `worldContext.ocean` reads no land beyond an open
   edge, `worldContext.monsoon` its continent's — never the map's own land extrapolated, so a land-heavy realm does not
   swing its own zone); the belt edges follow it (the subtropical highs at φ_I ± `subtropicalOffsetDeg`, the polar fronts at ±
   `polarFrontDeg`), and each cell takes its month's band from `winds` shifted by the zone's displacement — the trades
   with their equatorward component, the westerlies with their poleward one, the polar easterlies (a world's recipe may
   override the belts as before). **The thermal term:** over land a component `thermal.onshorePerDeciC` × (the month's
   land–sea temperature contrast within `landFetchKm`) blows onshore in the warm half-year and offshore in the cold;
   where it reverses a cell's wind by more than `monsoonReversalDeg` between the two solstice months and the wet
   half-year (step 6) holds more than `wetHalfShare` of its rain, the cell reads **monsoon** in its reason — at the
   continent rung emergent where the land mass straddles 10–30° of latitude; **at the realm and province rungs never
   emergent** (a 1 280 km map cannot make one; it can only receive one from a continent larger than itself): there
   the term reads `WorldRecipe.worldContext.monsoon` — the continent beyond the map by its side, size and latitude —
   as the land fraction beyond that edge, a `set` or `locked` requirement of kind `context` the dialog offers, and a
   monsoon inclusion asked for at those rungs without it is reported `W_MONSOON_CONTEXT` with the knob offered (file r
   choice (d)). Stored `windMonthCdeg[m]`, `windMonthStrength[m]`; `windCdeg` and `windStrength` the annual vector
   mean. The frame's `Terrain.wind` on a placed frame is the annual wind rotated into frame terms (V13 §3.11.5); the
   charter's `monthly` carries the months.
6. **Precipitation by the wind march, per month** (J-V13.112, J-V13.114). The march runs TWELVE times, once per
   month with that month's wind field (step 5), each run writing `precipMonthMm[m]`, the annual `precipMm` their sum.
   For each month, parcels march along each cell's wind direction across the coarse raster (a band is now the set of
   cells sharing the month's bearing; a curved field is marched cell by cell along its local direction, the nearer
   axis first, alternating, so every cell is visited once per month): a parcel starts at the upwind edge with
   moisture m = 0 plus a jitter drawn once per start row and month on `world.climate` (keyed by the row and the month;
   ± 10 %) — on a continuation (V13 §3.1 (6)) with the moisture and the maritime fraction the edge charter's station
   carries instead; at each water cell m += `pickupPerCellOverWater` ÷ 12 × (1 + `currents.pickupPerDeciC` × the
   cell's `sstAnomalyDeciC` ÷ 10) (warm water evaporates more, cold less: the coastal effect of step 6b); at each
   land cell the
   drop is d = `dropShare` × m + `orographicPerM` × max(0, rise) × m (rise the dem gain from the previous cell, in m),
   plus `coastalBonus` ÷ 12 at the first land cell after water; a rise of `barrierM` or more in one step dumps the
   whole parcel; a cell whose month's temperature is below the permafrost threshold receives half its drop; the cell's
   `precipMonthMm[m]` += d; m −= d; m += `recycleShare` × the cell's own month evaporation (step 7: moisture
   recycling, the part of a land cell's rain that falls again downwind). The **belt rains** are added per month beside
   the march, each scaled by the cell's maritime fraction: `convergenceMmPerMonth` within 8° of the month's φ_I,
   `frontalMmPerMonth` in the month's westerlies band, `convectiveMmPerMonth` over land in its warm half-year. A
   diagonal wind marches along the nearer axis then the other, alternating, so every cell is visited once per month.
   Results clamped per month to 3 × `rainCapMm` ÷ 12 and per year to `rainCapMm`. The march with an orographic drop and a rain shadow is
   the reference's mechanism in its own words (`research/fmg/FMG-survey.md` §"The physical pipeline", *Climate*, as
   evidence; its axis-aligned winds and unspecified 0–255 scale are what the arbitrary bearing and the mm/yr unit
   replace).
6b. **The ocean currents, per basin and month** (F4; J-V13.113; the spine's §8). Over each connected ocean basin
   (`basin`: the ocean feature's cells, split where a strait narrower than one coarse cell closes it) W3 solves the
   barotropic stream function ψ on the coarse grid for each month — β ∂ψ/∂x = curl(τ_m) ÷ (ρ H) − r ∇²ψ + A ∇⁴ψ, with
   τ_m the month's wind stress (∝ `windMonthStrength`² along `windMonthCdeg`), β = `currents.betaEqPerM` × cos(lat),
   A = `viscosityM2s`, r = `drag`; ψ = 0 on the mainland coast and a constant per island fixed by its circulation
   condition — at the **continent** rung; at the **realm and province rungs** (a realm spans ≈ 7° of latitude and
   cannot make a gyre that spans 15°–45°: it receives one from an ocean larger than the map, exactly as the monsoon)
   the solve runs only over enclosed seas wholly inside the map, while an open ocean beyond an edge is
   `WorldRecipe.worldContext.ocean` — the basin side the map's coast faces and its latitude span — whose coast anomaly
   and along-shore current come from the rule-based coast-facing table (an east coast of a basin: a warm poleward
   current; a west coast between 15° and 35°: a cold equatorward current with upwelling; else neutral — the science
   note's §4.4, its first method), and at an open edge ψ takes the context's value as a fixed row, never a wall;
   `cycles` multigrid V-cycles in row-major order through `dmath` — and reads u = −∂ψ/∂y, v = ∂ψ/∂x into
   `currentMonth[m]`: in every basin bounded east and west a subtropical gyre with a narrow, fast western boundary
   current and a broad, slow eastern one, an opposite subpolar gyre poleward of it, the equatorial currents under the
   trades with their countercurrent, a circumpolar current where a latitude band is unbroken by land (the western
   boundary's width ≈ (A ÷ β)^⅓ ≈ 50 km, which the coarse grid resolves at every rung). **The coastal effect:** a
   coast cell's `sstAnomalyDeciC` is `sstWarmDeciC` × the share of an along-shore poleward current on a western
   boundary (an east coast), `sstColdDeciC` × the share of an equatorward one on an eastern boundary (a west coast),
   plus `upwellingDeciC` where the along-shore wind drives the surface offshore (the trades on a west coast between
   15° and 35°), fading over `coastalReachKm` inland and seaward; step 2 reads it into the month's temperature and
   step 6 into the pickup — so a cold-upwelling coast is a desert coast and a warm-current coast a humid one. The
   solve is global over a basin (an elliptic problem has no local dirty set), and a land↔water change moves the thermal
   term's land–sea contrast and the convergence zone's swing, hence every month's wind stress over every basin: a relief
   or water edit re-solves every basin (V13 §3.14.2, §3.8 (12); J393); a `paintLayer` of `current` holds its cells' vectors through every solve (an always-so
   override, V13 §3.14.1). On a continuation the stream function along an open-sea edge is the edge charter's (V13
   §3.1 (6)). *Budget:* ≈ 30 / 120 / 260 ms per world at the three rungs for the twelve solves (V13 §6).
7. **Evaporation, per month:** `evapMonthMm[m]` = `evap.baseMm` ÷ 12 × clamp((T_m − `zeroAtDeciC`) ÷ (`fullAtDeciC`
   − `zeroAtDeciC`), 0, 1); `evapMm` their sum (the monthly values are transient: W4 reads the annual, step 6's
   recycling and the cover fold re-evaluate the month they need from `tempMonthDeciC`).

*Derive-only mode* (the import): with `tempDeciC` and `precipMm` given and no months, W3 runs steps 1, 3 (the former
distance-to-ocean continentality), 4 (the annual sinusoid at V13 §2.3's phases), 5 and 7 only, writes the twelve
months as the annual split by the sinusoid (temperature) and evenly (precipitation), solves no current, and W5 reads
the matrix path (V13 §3.6 (1)). *Output:*
the climate raster with one `ReasonRecord` per chunk (the rule, the slices, the winds read); a cell's reason — the band and the parcel's moisture at arrival — is `whyCell`'s on-demand re-evaluation (V13 §2.2). *Edges:* a world with no
water cell receives only the start jitter's moisture — a desert — and is reported; a `latBox` crossing the equator gives
both hemispheres' phases; a continent-rung world with one ocean basin and no strait solves one gyre; a realm- or
province-rung world's open sea reads its context's coast current and no gyre of its own; a basin of fewer than four
coarse cells carries no current (0) and no anomaly; a `worldContext.monsoon` on a continent-rung world is read beside the
emergent term and reported as redundant; a month whose wind field has no upwind edge for a row (a closed island
climate) starts that row's parcel at the first water cell.

### 3.5 W4 Regional hydrology

The site package's mechanism (§2.3's *The hydrology grid* and *Flats*, §4.2 S1 (3)) run at the world cell size on the
fine dem — the lifted core of `@plat/world/hydro` (BCR-V13-1), the same functions `@plat/site` calls, so the world's
flood and the frame's are one implementation (J-V13.9).

**3.5.1 Flow.** The priority flood fills every depression not a lake (lakes keep their surface as a flat at the spill
height), the two-gradient flat resolution writes `flatRank`, D8 in the fixed neighbour order E, NE, N, NW, W, SW, S, SE
writes `flowDir` on every land cell (frame and margin have no meaning here: the extent is the world), ties broken as
§2.3 states; the border is an outlet (an off-map exit). The filled levels go into the drainage arrays only, never into
`dem` (§7.3 (a) 2's rule), so a hollow the recipe dug stays a hollow and drains to its spill.

**3.5.2 Accumulation, discharge, lakes.** Runoff per cell r = `runoffShare` × max(0, `precipMm` − `evapMm`) × cell area
÷ `secondsPerYear` ÷ 1 000 (m³/s; a 1 km cell at 800 − 500 mm gives 0.0043 m³/s); `flowAccum` is the cell count and the
discharge the running sum of r downstream along D8 in descending `flatRank`-ordered height (one pass). A lake's inflow
is the sum of the discharge entering its cells; its `open` and `subtype` are V13 §3.3 (3)'s; an open lake passes its
inflow less evaporation on from its spill cell (the outlet), a closed lake passes nothing. The **carve**: where a reach
(below) runs, the dem under its course is lowered to a monotone bed by the site package's rule (§4.2 S1 (3): the bed
descends to the outlet, capped at the row's `carveMaxCm`, here `world.hydro.carveMaxCm` (V13 §2.3); a cell that would
need more keeps the flood's level and is reported `W_WORLD_SINK_UNRESOLVED`), each cell's cut recorded in
`carveDeltaCm` (item 140 M2); D8 is recomputed on the corridor cells and their neighbours and accumulation once, as S1 (3)
does.

**3.5.3 Reaches.** A **reach** is a maximal D8 chain of cells whose discharge ≥ `riverMinM3s`, cut at every confluence
(a cell receiving two such chains: the larger-discharge chain continues, the smaller ends into it as `to`), at a lake
(the chain ends `to` the lake; the lake's outlet starts a new reach `from` the lake) and at the sea or the border (an
exit). Its `course` is the cell centres smoothed by `chaikinPasses` Chaikin passes (the ends fixed); its per-vertex
`dischargeM3s` the cell's; `widthCm` = 100 × `width.a` × Q^`width.b`, `depthCm` = 100 × `depth.c` × Q^`depth.f`
(hydraulic geometry: the downstream relations' exponents are public, the coefficients ours); its `stageSurface` a
`WaterSurface` of kind `reach` whose `elevationCm` at each vertex is the carved bed + `depthCm` (bankfull); `navigable`
by `navigableM3s` at its downstream end; `mouth` by V13 §2.3's rule where it ends at a sea or lake; `exitHeadCm` at a
border exit. A **delta** splits the last `deltaReachKm` of the course into 2–3 distributaries by the site package's
delta rule at world scale (§4.2 S1 (3) *Mouths*; the shares drawn on `water.delta` keyed by the reach, the one draw of
W4); an **estuary** widens the width profile linearly over the last reach to `estuaryWidenShare` ×. Names come from W9.
The reach's reason names its source cell, its discharge inputs (precipitation, evaporation, runoff share, area) and the
width law's cells.

**3.5.4 The groundwater field and springs.** Over the fine grid: every surface cell (sea, lake, reach course cell) is a
source at its surface's elevation; a multi-source Dijkstra (the lifted bucket queue of `@plat/world/hydro`, C13-44)
spreads outward over land cells with the edge cost = the step's length in m × g(cell), g = `gradientBase` × (`precipMm`
÷ `precipRefMm`) × `permeability[geology]`; the **uncapped table** at a cell = min over sources of (source elevation +
accumulated rise) — it may reach and exceed the ground (C13-47); the **stored** `tableCm` is min(the uncapped table,
dem − `minDepthCm`) — `minDepthCm` the basement reading's floor, never the spring test's; on an `impermeable` cell the
stored table is min(that, dem − `perchDepthCm`) (the perched table; a world
with no impermeable cell never reads it, and a frame whose charter's geology mode is not impermeable reports
`W_GW_PERCHED_IGNORED` when its own geology op says otherwise). `source[cell]` records the winning source cell (the
clerk's "set by the river's surface 40 m away"). **Springs:** a land cell that is no surface cell, whose **uncapped**
table ≥ dem − `springMarginCm`, whose `flowAccum` ≥ `springMinAccumCells` and whose `flowDir` leads downhill is a
candidate; candidates
are thinned to one per `springSpacingM` in descending (table − dem), ties by cell index; each spring's `flowM3s` is the
discharge of its cell. The field costs what accumulation costs (one queue pass over the land cells). The frame-scale
field is the same function over `Terrain.hydro` (V13 §3.12.3). The rule — a table rising inland from the nearest
surface by recharge and permeability, capped by the ground, perched where the rock says — is the proposal's
(`proposal-hydrology-water-state.md` §2 (3)) stated here once in full; the reference has no groundwater
(`fmg-physical-pipeline.md` §3.12 as evidence of the gap).

**3.5.5 Distance fields and watersheds.** `distToShoreM` and `distToRiverM` are true Euclidean distance transforms
(the two-pass method over the fine grid, in metres); `watershed` labels every land cell with the id of the `Watershed`
whose outlet its D8 path reaches (a sea cell, a lake, or a border cell — an `edge` basin with `exitHeadCm`), its
`areaKm2` the cell count × the cell area.

*Output:* the drainage arrays, `carveDeltaCm`, the reaches and their surfaces, the lakes' `open`, `subtype` and
`outlet`, the watersheds, the groundwater field, the distance fields. *Edges:* a world with no land has no reach and no
spring; one land cell is one basin draining to the sea; a reach of one cell (a spring at the shore) exists when its
discharge passes the threshold; a dem all at one height (a flat) resolves by `flatRank` to its border, as §2.3's flats
do; the ladders are V13 §3.16's.

### 3.6 W5 Biomes and resources

1. **The potential natural vegetation per fine cell** (J-V13.115). `biome` is the vegetation the climate would grow
   without people — the potential natural vegetation, the climate-level class the dossier's climate row names; never
   the land cover (step 5). **The classification path** (every generated world: a monthly climate present): for every
   land cell the twelve monthly temperatures and precipitations (bilinearly sampled from the coarse climate raster, the
   temperatures then moved to the fine cell's height: T_m,fine = T_m,sampled − `lapseDeciCPerKm` × (dem_fine −
   dem_coarse,sampled) ÷ 1 000 m, the coarse heights sampled with the temperatures they were lapsed at — so a peak
   inside a coarse cell reads its own climate, never its valley's)
   are classified by `world.koppen`'s thresholds (V13 §2.3) into a three-letter class — E first (the hottest month
   under 10 °C: ET where it is above 0, else EF), then B (the annual total under 10 × (2 × MAT in °C + the factor by which
   half-year holds ≥ 70 % of the rain): W under 5 ×, S above; h or k by MAT 18 °C), then A (the coldest month ≥ 18 °C:
   f, m or w by the driest month against 60 mm and 100 − MAP ÷ 25), C (the coldest month above `cdBoundaryDeciC`) and
   D (at or below it) with s, w or f by the dry season's month ratios and a, b, c or d by the summer's months — and
   the class is mapped by `world.pnv`'s rows to a `world.biomes` row (`Af` rainforest … `EF` ice; the row's `dryMargin`
   where the class sits within 10 % of its own arid threshold: a forest-steppe). The overrides run after, in this order
   and each final: a water cell takes `overrides.water` (the empty biome); a cell whose growing season — the months
   above `treelineGrowingSeasonDeciC` — is shorter than `growingSeasonMonths` is `alpine` (the treeline; the matrix
   path's `alpineAboveM` serves the import only); a cell whose `flowAccum` ≥ `wetlandAccumCells`, whose dem slope
   (the max over the eight neighbours of |Δdem| ÷ distance) is under `wetlandSlopeMax` and whose biome is not a desert
   is `wetland`; a cell within `riparianCells` of a reach through an arid class takes its nearest humid class's row (a
   gallery forest); a cell whose `soil` is in `overrides.edaphic` takes that row (a spodosol heath, a vertisol
   grassland); an `Override` of layer `biome` over the cell takes the painted row (always so, V13 §3.14.1). **The
   matrix path** (the import's derive-only mode, V13 §3.4, and a world older than this item): the matrix row
   `Recipe.world.biomeMatrix` (V13 §2.3) is read with the cell's mean temperature as the row index (the first
   `tempBands` bound the value is under) and its precipitation as the column index, the cell's biome `cells[row][col]`,
   the matrix's overrides (`alpineAboveM`, `permafrostBelowDeciC` unless the matrix already says `tundra`,
   `wetlandAccumCells`) as before — kept so an imported map with annual climate arrays classifies as it did, never
   taken for a generated world. Ties never arise: every threshold is strict. `landUse` is the biome row's — the
   potential cover's class, not a human use (step 5). No stream is drawn: W5's biome is a pure function of W3, W4 and
   the soil.
2. **Vegetation and habitability rasters** are the biome row's cells copied per fine cell (`vegetation`, `habitability`),
   kept as Uint8 (× 255) for the view and W6. A cell adjacent (8-neighbour) to a sea or lake cell raises habitability by
   `coastalHabitabilityBonus` (V13 §2.3; clamped to 1) — the shore is where people live.
3. **Resource sites.** A resource is a `ResourceSite` record (V13 §2.2)
   placed by rule rows of `world.resources` (TS block: `ResourceRule { kind: string /* an OPEN row id (J397 (M37)): the eight shipped (mundane) rows below, the example rows `silverVein`, `gemPipe` and `mageSpring`, and a DM's custom rows through the content volume's custom path (V11 §3.13; BCR-V13-55) — never a closed union */; label?: string /* the pin's word and the catalogue's glyph id; absent, the id */; where: { biome?: string[]; geology?: RecipeOp['geology']['kind'][]; bedrock?: string[] /* `world.formation`'s bedrock classes; read where a formation op ran, else the rule's `geology` */; soil?: string[] /* `world.soil`'s classes */; landUse?: string[]; coastal?: boolean; minSlopePct?: number; maxSlopePct?: number; minAccum?: number }; density: number /* sites per 1 000 km² of eligible cells */; spacingKm: number }`).
   Default rows (own; calibratable): `timber` — forest land use, density 6, spacing 8 km; `stone` — slope ≥ 8 %, or
   bedrock limestone, shield or folded belt, density 3, spacing 12; `ore` — bedrock arc volcanics, folded belt or
   shield (geology `volcanic` where no formation op ran), or slope ≥ 15 %, density 1.2, spacing 25; `salt` — coastal, a
   `saltLake` shore or bedrock evaporite, density 1, spacing 30; `clay` — slope ≤ 1 % and `flowAccum` ≥ 50, or soil
   vertisol, density 2, spacing 10; `fish` — coastal or a lake shore with `open`, density 4, spacing 6; `peat` —
   `wetland` or soil histosol, density 2, spacing 10; `pasture` — grass land use, density 4, spacing 8. The example
   rows (own; fantasy; shipped off in the parity presets; calibratable): `silverVein` — bedrock folded belt or shield,
   density 0.3, spacing 40; `gemPipe` — bedrock arc volcanics or young lava, density 0.1, spacing 60; `mageSpring` — a
   spring cell on soluble bedrock, density 0.2, spacing 50; a DM's custom row is one more of these, its glyph the
   symbol catalogue's under the blocklist lint (V11 §3.13). For each rule: the eligible cells are listed, the expected count is density × eligible area ÷
   1 000 km², candidates are drawn on `world.resources` (keyed by the world root and the rule's ordinal: a position-keyed
   draw per eligible cell, the lowest `count` draws kept, V13 §3.17) and thinned to one per `spacingKm` in draw order;
   `amount` is a second draw in [0.3, 1]. A resource's reason names the rule row, the eligibility terms that held and the
   draw key.
4. **The frame-scale projection.** A resource inside a placed frame's extent + margin enters the charter's `resources` in
   frame cm (V13 §3.11.4); the base's own siting term for resources (§4.2 S0's demand reading) reads them through the
   charter, never through the raster.

5. **Land cover — the campaign-time ecology, by the cover fold, never by W5** (F2, F3; the spine's §3; J-V13.116,
   J-V13.128). What the land looks like at a week — fields, pasture, coppice, fallow, scrub, regrowth, a burn scar,
   a flood's silt, ash — is not W5's and not a `WorldRaster` field: it is a **cover plate** (`CoverPlate`, V13 §2.2)
   folded by `WORLD_COVER` into the cover cache (`Document.coverPlates`, BCR-V13-41) at every lens window's fold (one
   plate per host advance, beside the lens plate), once at the campaign's creation from the populations `CampaignFacts`
   carries (the birth fold, V13 §5.8 (9); J397 (M1); the birth window's `sizes` winning where both are sent) and at
   every `disturb`, and read at view time by the `landCover`
   layer (V13 §5.1), `worldFactsAt` (V14's E1 crop; a placed frame's surroundings), `landCoverAt`, the settlement map
   record's `landCoverShare` and the `physicalChange` offer — by no stage of W0–W9, no sway revision, no encounter's
   generation and no canon (a lint, T-V13-62). **The law is a pure function, never a simulation:** cover(cell, week) =
   stage(the cell's potential vegetation, the cell's last dated event and its kind, week − that event's week, the use
   the dated host facts assign now), with no stepping, no stored trajectory and no draw — so a plate at week t equals
   its re-derivation, a dropped cache rebuilds, and the scrub reads any week (J384 (9)'s plates). Its inputs, all
   dated: **(a) human use** from the window's host facts — each bound seat's population and tier (`PolitySeat`,
   `LensFacts.sizes`; a standalone seat its tier band's median), the population CLAMPED to its tier's band ceiling
   (`use.bandCeiling`: the next tier's floor from the host's travel law where it sends its tier table, else the row's;
   J397 (M25) — the seat's size banded by tier, never raw population, so the fields are bounded on every horizon and a
   runaway seat's fields never flood its landmass), gives an area demand min(population, ceiling) ×
   `use.landPerPersonHaByTier` × (`cropShare` + `fallowShare`) for fields, × `pastureShare` for pasture and ×
   `woodlandShare` for coppice; the demand is met by cost-distance from the seat over the fine cost surface under the
   cost law's time terms at `use.walkKmH` with its slope term (roads and rivers cheaper), fields assigned to eligible
   cells in ascending travel time until the demand is met, with no time cap (a shortfall past `use.fieldHoursMax` (2) is
   reported in the seat's reason: at an eligible share of 30–50 % a seat of 10 000 fills a disc of 7–10 km) — a cell
   eligible when its soil's `fertility` ≥ `fertilityMin`, its slope ≤ `fieldSlopeMaxPct`, not water, wetland or ice,
   and not inside a placed frame's extent (the town's own ground is the frame's) —, pasture and coppice next, out to
   2 × `catchmentHours` (a shortfall reported), overlapping catchments split by nearest travel time (the partition W8a
   already computes); a seat's use is withdrawn by a dated host event — a razing, a plague's depopulation, an
   abandonment (`WorldEvent.kind` `razing`, `plagueDeaths` or `abandonment` by the adapter folder's event table), sent
   with the seat's population after it (`WorldEvent.populationAfter`, H34): the cells beyond the new demand take the event's week
   and kind — and, where no event is sent, **by the plates themselves** (J397 (M26)): each plate records per seat its
   demand count (`CoverPlate.demand`: the cells its use met, counted in the seat's fixed travel-time order), and a cell
   beyond the demand takes as its withdrawal week the week of the first plate in the series at which its rank exceeded
   the seat's count and stayed so to the plate asked (`withdrawal.dateBy`), entering the biome's `succession` from that
   week; a population change between events therefore moves the use's extent AND dates it, so the forest returns to a
   shrinking town's outer ring without an event the host does not mint; `fallow` is the rotation's stage of a field in
   use (the `fallowShare`), never a permanent class; the function stays pure
   in (the potential vegetation, the last dated event, the weeks since, the dated series of demand counts, the use the
   facts assign now) and a dropped
   cache rebuilds in one fill per dated event plus one integer scan per seat over the series (`WORLD-17`; SP-W11); **(b) disturbances** — every `Disturbance` (a DM's stamp, or a host
   event the DM attributed) sets its cells' event kind and week; **(c) succession and recovery** — a cell with an event
   reads `world.cover`'s `recovery` sequence for (kind, biome) at week − event week — the kinds OPEN rows of that table
   (J397 (M37)): the shipped mundane rows, the example rows (a blight, a curse-scar, a wild-magic zone, each with a
   recovery law of its own) and a DM's custom rows through the content volume's custom path (V11 §3.13), never a closed
   union, so fantasy is a row with its own recovery and never an always-so paint with none —, a cell whose use was withdrawn the
   `succession` sequence for its biome, a cell in use its use class, any other cell its potential vegetation's own
   class; an `Override` of layer `landCover` holds its cells' class through every fold (always so). **Land cover is
   never the dossier's biome:** the dossier holds the climate-level class (W5's `biome` → V11's `ClimateRow`);
   clearing and regrowth never raise the conflict list (V13 §3.11.5 (1)) and only a change of `biome` can (T-V13-62).
   The fold's budget is V13 §6's cover row; its reason records are per plate chunk. *Edges:* a standalone world with no
   seats folds a plate equal to the potential vegetation; a seat with no population sent uses its tier's median; a
   disturbance before the first window dates from its own week; a cell both in use and disturbed reads the disturbance
   until its recovery reaches the use's class, then the use; a seat's catchment on an island smaller than its demand
   takes the island and reports the shortfall in the seat's reason.

*Output:* `biome` (the potential natural vegetation), `landUse`, `vegetation`, `habitability` rasters; the resource
sites; the cover plates (the fold's, V13 §2.6). *Edges:* a world with one biome
(a matrix row of one cell) places every resource whose rule it satisfies; a rule with no eligible cell places none and is
not reported (an absence is a fact). The biome idea — a climate matrix with overrides — is the reference's as evidence
(V13 §2.3); the resource rule is own (the reference has no resources, `FMG-survey.md` §"The physical pipeline").

### 3.7 W6 Suitability and siting proposals

W6 answers three callers with one function: the standalone world (where do settlements belong), the host (a demand
for *n* sites of a kind — item 134 (c)'s site-makes-the-ground rule and the proposal's demand message) and V14's G3
(a site's purpose weights). It never creates a settlement; it writes `SitingProposal`s the user, the host or V14's G3
accept. **W6 is two stages** (C13-33: W6 and W7 read each other, so each is split and the four run W6a → W7a → W6b →
W7b in the declared I/O): **W6a** writes `proposals.stage1` from the raster below; **W7a** routes over them (V13 §3.8);
**W6b** reads `routes.stage1`, adds the `connectivity` term and writes `proposals`; **W7b** routes over the final seats.

**The plug-in** (C13-19; SW-01; V13 §2.2's `SuitabilityTerm`, `SuitabilityContext`, `terms.register`, `score`):
`@plat/world/siting` holds the registry `terms` of named terms, each a pure, deterministic function of a cell and the
context; W6a and W6b call `score(cell, ctx, weights, hard?)` with `world.suitability`'s weights; V14's G3 calls it
with its purpose row's weights and `hard` terms (a hard term's zero refuses the cell); the host calls it through
`proposals`. **The registry holds V13's eight generic terms (below); V14 registers its purpose terms (V14 §2.5)
through `terms.register(term)` and they are V14's to state** — this volume defines none of them (J-V13.51). The
context carries everything a plug-in may read (the rasters, the coast, the reaches and surfaces, the routes, the
placements, the site placements, the resources, the springs, the territories, the wet-season stage of a reach). No
term, V13's or V14's, draws: the score has no random or jitter term (item 132 (b)'s "derived, never random", extended
to siting; SW-03; J-V13.53).

1. **The score raster, stage 1 (W6a).** For every land cell `c`: `score1(c) = Σ_t w_t · term_t(c)` over the
   `SuitabilityRule.weights` terms except `connectivity`; every term in [0, 1]:
   - `habitability`: the biome row's × (0.5 + 0.5 × the cell's soil class's `fertility`, `world.soil`) — the soil
     enters the existing term, never a ninth generic term (J-V13.51's eight stand; file r choice (l)); a world with
     no formation op reads fertility 0.6 everywhere (the `inceptisol` row), so its scores are the former ones scaled.
   - `discharge`: min(1, Q ÷ `discharge.refM3s`) where Q is the largest reach discharge within one fine cell (0 off
     a reach); a cell *on* a navigable reach adds `navigableBonus` before the clamp.
   - `lowland`: 1 − min(1, (dem − the nearest surface's level) ÷ (`lowland.refM` × 100)) — low ground near water
     reads 1, a plateau 500 m above its river 0.
   - `coastType`: the rule's value for the cell's coast class: `none` if `distToShoreM` > one fine cell; else `bay` when
     the shore cell's feature is a bay (W2's enclosed-water class: a sea cell whose eight-neighbour land count ≥ 5, own),
     `estuary` when within `world.hydro.mouth.estuaryReachKm` of an estuary mouth, `lake` on an `open` lake, `saltLake`
     on a closed one, else `open`.
   - `resource`: min(1, Σ amount of resource sites within `reach.resourceKm` ÷ 2).
   - `spring`: 1 when a spring lies within one fine cell, 0.5 within three, else 0.
   - `destination` (the world-site term, named so everywhere — V13 §2.3's weight key and `reach.siteKm`; SW-01): the
     placed world sites' pull: Σ over site placements within `reach.siteKm` of the card's `attraction` (0–1, read
     through the resolver) × (1 − d ÷ reach), clamped — the owner's item 134 (c): a site makes the ground around it
     worth settling.
   A cell on water, on `ice`, or above the size row's `reliefLimitM` scores 0. The raster is transient (V13 §2.4).
2. **Spacing passes.** Two passes pick candidates from the raster in descending score, ties by cell index: the *capital*
   pass with `spacing.capitalKm` and a target count `capitals` = max(1, ⌊land km² ÷ `spacing.capitalPerKm2`⌋), then
   the *town* pass with `spacing.townKm` and target `towns` = ⌊land km² ÷ `spacing.townPerKm2`⌋. A pass that places
   fewer than `spacing.targetShare` × its target multiplies its spacing by `spacing.shrink` and repeats, at most four times;
   a pass that still places fewer reports `W_SITING_SPARSE`. A candidate is refused when any accepted candidate lies
   within the spacing (a Euclidean test over an accepted-cell grid bucketed at the spacing).
3. **Port promotion.** A candidate on an `open`, `bay` or `estuary` coast whose landmass has another candidate across
   water (a sea route would exist, W7's water legs) has its score × `portPromote`; the highest-scoring port candidate per
   landmass is a `harbourCandidate`, as is every candidate with a navigable reach whose coast type is not `none` (on a
   standalone world the harbour itself; on a host-bound world a suggestion — the host's port rule joins the geography
   half, every proposal's `WaterAccess`, to its own institution half and keeps the verdict; J-V13.74); **a water body
   with fewer than `minPortsPerBody` port candidates on its shores gets none** (a sea route needs two ends; the
   reference's two-ports rule kept, C13-51). This is the reference's idea of ports and the harbour score restated as our
   own law (`FMG-survey.md` §"Burgs and states", as evidence); the terms and the two-pass spacing are own.
4. **Stage 2 (W6b, connectivity).** After W7a has run over the stage-1 candidates, each candidate's `connectivity`
   term is min(1, routes of `routes.stage1` touching its cell ÷ `stage2.connectivityRefRoutes`) and `score2 = score1 +
   w_connectivity · connectivity`; candidates are re-ranked by `score2` and the spacing passes re-applied over the
   ranked list (never adding, only dropping a candidate now out-ranked within spacing); W7b then routes over the final
   list. One iteration only (J-V13.10: a second changes under 2 % of seats in the spike's trial, V13 §8.3).
5. **The host's demand, and the included settlements' requirements.** `proposals(world, demand)` (the port, V13
   §3.11.6) takes `{ kind: 'capital'|'town'|'port'|'site'; count; near?: WorldPointCm; withinKm?; weights?:
   Partial<SuitabilityRule['weights']>; exclude?: Id[]; requirements?: Requirement[] /* the settlement's facts as hard
   terms: a `coast` row refuses a cell whose coast type is `none`, a `river` row a cell with no reach within one fine
   cell, a `lake` row a cell off a lake shore, a `climateRow` row a cell whose potential vegetation's climate row lies
   more than one band from it, a `latitude` row a cell outside the band, a `terrain` row a cell outside the relief
   class (the `dossier` term's readings, V13 §3.11.1) */ }`; it re-scores with the merged weights, applies the
   requirements as hard terms (a refused cell scores 0), restricts to the disc or, with no `near`, to the whole map,
   drops `exclude` and the cells within the current placements' spacing, and returns the top `count` as proposals with
   `demand` set to the host's key and each proposal's requirement readings in its reason. The default weights are the
   table's; a host's weights never persist (an input to one call, recorded in each proposal's reason). W6 never reads
   a dossier itself: the facts arrive as requirements (`CampaignFacts`, V13 §3.11.6), and a run with `include` set
   scores every planned site of V13 §3.1 (5) under its settlement's rows, so the standalone world's own seats and the
   included settlements' sites are one scoring. **The host's one-button placer** — the host's one-button placement of its
   settlements with its mismatch popup — becomes a caller of `placeFrame`'s best form (V13 §3.11.1: the whole-map
   search under the settlement's requirements, the three offers, organic correction only when none is lawful) through
   the port, never a second scorer (H31; J-V13.120).
6. **The proposal record.** Each `SitingProposal` carries its terms as `terms` (each term's value), its `score`, `port`,
   its `cell` and `at` (the cell centre) and a reason naming the pass, the spacing in force and the rule slice's digest.
   **The one tie-break of siting, stated once for every caller** (SW-03; V14 cites it): two candidates of equal
   score are ordered by the lowest cell index, then by the lexicographic order of their ids — no draw; `world.siting`
   is a reserved concern id with no stream.

*Output:* the proposals; the standalone world's seats are the capital-pass proposals (W8 reads them as
`Recipe.world.seats` when the recipe gave none). *Edges:* a world with one land cell proposes it; a world with no land
proposes none (F-WORLD rung "none placed": reported, every later stage runs empty); a host demand of `count` 0 returns
none and is not an error.

### 3.8 W7 Routes (W7a over the stage-1 candidates, W7b over the final seats; C13-33)

1. **The seats.** The route graph's nodes are the seats: every `Placement` (a placed frame's origin mapped to its fine
   cell), every host seat with a position (through the port), every stage-1 or final proposal when W7 runs for W6, and
   every site placement whose card is flagged `routed` (V14 §2.5's kind row, copied at the drop; SW-20). A seat's rank is its tier (a placement's frame tier; a proposal's pass:
   capital 2, town 1, port + 1; a site 0).
2. **The cost surface.** Per fine cell, the land step cost from cell `a` to its neighbour `b` over distance `d` m (the
   cell size, × √2 on a diagonal): `d × perM × (1 + slopePerPct × slope%) × biomeFactor[biome(b)]`, slope% = |dem(b) −
   dem(a)| ÷ d × 100; + `riverCrossing` when the step crosses a reach ≥ `riverMinM3s` that neither cell's reach carries
   (a crossing, not a run along the bank); × `existingRoute` when `b` already carries a route (the share of cells that
   gain a second route is what makes roads converge — the reference's idea, as evidence, `FMG-survey.md` §"Routes"; the
   law is the host's as data, V13 §2.3, our default rows); a water cell costs `waterPerM` (∞: impassable) on a land leg.
   A water leg (sea or navigable reach) costs `seaPerM` or `navigableRiverPerM` per metre over water cells only, and may
   start and end only at a harbour seat when `portOnly` — on a standalone world a W6 `harbourCandidate`, on a host-bound
   world the port seats the host's genesis water edges name — (a non-port seat reaches the sea by a land leg to the
   nearest port).
3. **The neighbour graph.** The seats of one landmass are joined by the Urquhart graph of their Delaunay triangulation
   (the longest edge of every triangle removed: own choice over the full triangulation — fewer, more plausible pairs;
   J-V13.11), computed by the kernel's deterministic triangulation (§5.1's primitive) over the seats' positions handed to
it in **integer metres** (`originCm ÷ 100`, rounded; the continent rung's far corner at 3.84 × 10⁶ m lies inside §3.2
(1)'s range invariant of 2²³ at every rung), the edges read back by seat id — no world cm reaches a kernel predicate
(SW-16). Pairs across
   water are joined only when both are ports (the sea graph: the same Urquhart rule over port seats, per sea), plus the
   reference's sea-route vocabulary kept as own rules (C13-51): when `sea.trunk`, every landmass with ≥ `minPortsPerBody`
   ports gets one **trunk** sea leg from its highest-ranked port to the nearest port of the largest landmass; and a port
   pair whose sea cost ≤ `sea.gapFixRatio` × its land cost gets the sea leg beside the land one (the **gap fix**).
4. **The paths.** Edges are processed in descending rank (the higher seat's rank first, ties by the pair's sorted
   lineage keys); each edge is one **A\*** run (the lifted bucket queue with integer costs — the cost × 1 000 rounded —
   and the straight-line cost at `landBase × perM` as the heuristic, admissible under the cost law since no cell is
   cheaper than level open ground; ties by (f, cell index), so deterministic; C13-36) from its lower seat to its higher
   over the cost surface, **confined to the ellipse** of cells whose straight cost from both seats ≤ `maxCostFactor` ×
   the pair's straight cost (the drop rule already bounds the answer), with the `existingRoute` discount applied against
   the routes already laid — so later roads ride earlier ones; the polyline is the cell-centre path simplified by
   Visvalingam's area rule at `routeToleranceM` (as the base simplifies its coast; C13-44) and never crossing a water
   cell on a land leg (the simplification rejects a shortcut that leaves land). A path whose cost exceeds `maxCostFactor`
   × the straight-line cost at `landBase` is dropped (F-WORLD rung "no path": the pair stays unjoined and is reported
   `W_ROUTE_NO_PATH`, never a route through the sea).
5. **Classes.** The first `classes.primaryShare` of land edges by the higher seat's rank are `highway`, the rest `road`;
   an edge both of whose seats are rank 0 is `track`; every seat still unjoined after the passes gets a `trail` to its
   nearest routed cell (one Dijkstra to the route set); water legs are `sea` or `river`. A cell's `route` layer is the
   set of route ids crossing it (the charter reads it at the frame's edge, V13 §3.11.4).
6. **The reason** per route names its ends, its class rule, the cost total and the three largest cost contributions
   (slope, biome, crossing) — the clerk's "the road bends here because the pass is 400 m lower".
7. **The host's law and the stations.** Under the host's cost law the step cost of (2) reads `classFactor` for
   `biomeFactor`, adds `riverCellAdd` on a river cell and multiplies a step above `elevationKneeM` by
   `elevationKneeFactor`; `existingRoute`, `maxCostFactor` and the classes are lay rules (`world.routeLay`) and never
   enter a time. After every pass each route's integer fields are evaluated on its final polyline, order-free:
   `landEffortM` under the time terms, `lengthM`, the water metres by kind, `byClassM`, the crossings, the per-vertex
   `stations` and `vertexClass`, and the 52-week seasonal sets (J-V13.73).
8. **Genesis at world birth (a host-bound world).** The host's generation path places its founding members through
   the port, derives its genesis network over the seats and the edges the map lays at creation under its own law and sends one
  frozen `RouteGenesis` record (V13 §3.11.6), whose costs enter the canon at the first advance (the grace rule, V13
  §3.11.6; H12, H22, H38; J397 (M2)) — on a campaign born on this world no canon exists at birth, so the network is
  laid over the seats as they then stand and re-laid at each grace drag. W7 then lays **exactly those edges**, in host-key order, with the host's grades: no pair
   selection, no rank classes, no trails to host seats, a water edge as one water route between its two port seats;
   (1)–(5)'s own selection runs only on a standalone world, and a standalone world's routes among seats later bound to a
   host are tombstoned at binding. A campaign whose host has no genesis keeps its drawn roads as presentation only — and so does every host-bound world until the host's genesis network lands: that network is the host's own route-network mount, which records the `genesis` this module lays at creation as its input (one record, no second mount recording it) and lands after the host's release (J400 (7); V13 §8.5's H12); until then the roads are laid and drawn as here and read by nothing the host simulates.
9. **The lived network, mirrored, never computed.** `network(world, window, changes)` folds the host's route changes
   by window: only `chartered` lays new geometry (its course hint honoured, the course correction a recorded geometry);
   a demotion keeps the polyline; a revival restores the hidden one; a `bypass` (the host's detour round a seat it
   avoids: the avoided seat and its radius) re-lays the route round that radius under the cost law as a dated lay
   version under the same host key, the former lay kept and the hysteresis the host's; a hidden land road is a DM-only
   ghost and a hidden
   water lane a quiet-quay mark; a grade edit on a host route is refused (`refuse.world.hostRoute`) — the DM charters
   through the host's own command from the world editor, the world offering a read-only path preview. The route layer,
   the frame's road rows (`roadsAt(placement, week)`) and siting read the network at the week; a hidden road counts as no
   public road.
10. **After birth nothing moves a bound route silently.** W7 on a host-bound world is incremental: it lays only edges a
   host change names; a *this happened* edit re-lays a route from its week as a dated lay version the host may adopt as
   a live overlay; an *always so* edit, a recipe op, an adjust or a regenerate mints a lay version adopted only by the
   host's re-canonize (`W_HOST_CANON_BEHIND` until then); every route outside the edit's transitive closure (the
   triangles a changed seat alters, then every route whose search ellipse meets a cell whose route layer changed, to a
   fixed point) stays byte-identical, and the dry run names the closure.
11. **Legs end at settlements.** On a host-bound world every host route ends at two host settlements; a site, a
   proposal or a junction is a position along a route, never an end, so dropping or removing a site changes a route's
   geometry and effort, never the number of legs. A placed frame's exits are W7's terminals: a highway or road meets
   the town at its gate station after `exitRunM` through the margin, and `requestCharter` lays the town's own links
   before the charter is emitted.

12. **Sail routing: every sea leg priced by direction, month and vessel kind** (F4; the spine's §8; J-V13.125). A
   water leg's cost in (2) — `seaPerM` over water cells — is the host's symmetric law and stays the canon's; beside it
   W7 prices each water route's **sailing legs** (`SailingLeg`, V13 §2.2; `WorldRoute.sailing`) over the climate's
   monthly winds and currents (V13 §3.4 (5), (6b)): for each vessel kind of `world.sailing`, each month and each
   direction, a time-dependent shortest path over a **sea routing grid** of `routingGridKm` cells (16 km: the coarse
   ocean cells aggregated, refined to the coarse cell within three cells of each port and in a strait narrower than two
   routing cells) with `headings` headings per cell, where a step's cost is its length ÷ its ground-speed share — the
   vessel's polar at the angle between the heading and the month's true wind (0 where the rig cannot hold the course)
   less the leeway's drift, the ground speed solving the heading whose water velocity plus `currentCoupling` × the
   current's vector makes good the step's track (the vector sum, the cross-track part crabbed out) — a step no heading
   can make good at `minGroundShare` is impassable that month —, + `tackPenaltyMin`
   per heading change against the wind (a beat is a zig-zag of close-hauled headings the graph admits, each paying its
   penalty — so a square rig dead to windward makes about a tenth of its fair speed, often nothing, and the search
   prefers a longer course with the wind abeam, as sailors did) and `wearPenaltyMin` per gybe; an oared vessel's
   `oarKn` is its floor at every angle; a `coastal` vessel, or one with `nightStop`, steps only within
   `maxDaysFromShore` of a coast and pays `coastalFactor`; on a standalone world the month's `closedRisk` multiplies the
   whole leg (never an effort offered to the host, J393). A\* with
   the straight line ÷ the fair speed as the admissible heuristic, the lifted bucket queue with integer costs (cost ×
   1 000) and (f, cell index) ties: deterministic, no random weather (storms stay the host's storm season, multiplied
   in the host's own arithmetic). The result per (leg, vessel, month, direction) is an integer **sea effort-metre**
   count (the leg's length ÷ its mean ground-speed share) and the laid course where it differs from `polyline` — so
   outbound and return may differ in course and in cost (the same pair of ports differs by a factor of 3–7 with and
   against the prevailing system, the historical record this volume's cells are anchored on, T-V13-67), and sailing
   windows emerge from the months (a monsoon route out in summer and home in winter; a sea closed in winter).
   **What the host gets (J393):** `TravelEdge`, the canon's water metres and `WorldRoute.stations`, `openSeaM` and
   `coastalM` stay GEOMETRIC water metres, byte-identical before and after this item lands (T-V13-67) — the host prices
   them by its own sea speed as before, and no host time moves the day M-W9 lands; `routeFacts` offers, per host water
   edge and behind the host's own switch, the directional seasonal efforts by vessel and their **symmetric mean** (the
   mean of the twelve monthly efforts both ways; H33), each carrying wind and current only (never this volume's
   closed-season multiplier: storms stay the host's storm season, applied once in the host's arithmetic), and the host
   adopts them by its own law and its own re-canonize; until then every time the host shows is its own. **Laziness and
   budget:** a sailing leg is derived on demand per lane and cached in `derived` per (lane, geometry version, climate
   version) — the one-click path computes no sailing leg (the canon's water metres are geometric); the full twelve ×
   three × two set, and the symmetric mean from it, runs when the month slider, a lens's sea link or `routeFacts` asks
   (`WORLD-18`). **A strait edit** (a `strait` op, a `setField` that opens or closes a passage, a sea-level
   `setSurface`) re-solves every basin's currents (V13 §3.4 (6b)) and re-derives every sailing leg whose course crosses the changed cells, each changed
   leg's efforts before and after in the dry run's `timeDelta` with its band crossings (`W_TRAVEL_BAND_CROSSED`;
   `W_SAIL_LEG_CHANGED` names the legs) — never silently. **The lens rule:** a lens drawing a sea link (a sea column,
   a shipment, a plague's crossing) draws it along the host's own lane and prices it by the host's own leg unless the
   host adopted the directional efforts (V13 §5.8 (5)); the map never shows a traveller faster or slower than the
   host's clock says.

*Output:* `WorldRoute`s (with `sailing` on water routes) and the `route` layer. *Edges:* one seat: no route; two seats on separate landmasses, neither a
port: no route (reported); a seat on an island of one cell: a trail of length 0 is not made (the seat is its own route
end). W7 at the continent rung is the stage's cost driver (V13 §6).

### 3.9 W8 Polity — the seat territory (W8a) and the sway (W8b)

**Two partitions, never one** (J-V13.63; the owner's territory rules (T1)–(T3) and J382, V13 §1.3). W8 makes two things
that must not be confused. **W8a, the seat territory**, is the host's meaning of *territory*: every reachable land cell
belongs to the seat it is cheapest to reach, with no budget and no politics — the substrate of the host's distances,
frozen with them, in the canon's travel slot (V13 §3.11.6). **W8b, the sway**, is the picture of the host's political
facts over that ground: how far each settlement's reach runs before it fades, who holds which land, where two hostile
powers' reaches meet in a debatable land, which land no one holds. The sway is derived, revisioned and drawn; it is never
a fact of the map, never in the canon, and the host's crossings and distances never come from it.

**W8a — the seat territory.**
1. **Seeds.** One per member seat: every placed frame whose placement carries a `hostKey`, every host seat with a
   position (`bindSeat`, `importSeats`), on a standalone world every `RecipeSeat` (else the capital-pass proposals). A
   satellite of the host, a world site, a phantom and a dead settlement's remnant add nothing: W8a's membership follows
   the host's exactly (V13 §2.5).
2. **The flood.** One multi-source Dijkstra (the lifted bucket queue) over the **coarse** raster from every seed under
   the cost law's time terms (`RouteCostLaw`, the host's on a host-bound world), no budget, total over each landmass's
   reachable land; a cell goes to the seat that reaches it cheapest, ties by the lower cell index then the lower
   predecessor. A seed on water or ice moves to its nearest land cell (`W_POLITY_SEAT_MOVED`).
3. **Crossings.** For every pair of adjacent seat territories the cheapest crossing is found on the coarse boundary and
   refined on the fine grid inside its coarse cell: its world point, its two side points, the two crossing cells'
   terrain classes (the adapter folder's class table) and each side's integer cost from its seat — the canon's
   `TravelEdge`s. An imported legacy world keeps each of the host's own gates as a `HostGateRef` (V13 §3.15 (3)).
4. **Outputs and clock.** One `Territory` per seat (coarse cells, crossings, border, pole, neighbours), the coarse
   `territory` raster, the canon's travel slot. W8a changes only when its membership or the cost law changes — what the
   host adopts by its re-canonize (V13 §3.11.6) — and every sway revision, death, resettlement and satellite founding
   leaves it byte-identical (T-V13-41 (b)).

**W8b — the sway** (integer and draw-free; every coefficient a `world.polity` cell, V13 §2.3).
5. **Inputs.** The latest `PolityFacts` window of a host-bound world (V13 §2.2): seats with tier, size third,
   prosperity rung, force band, strength band and garrison presence; links in the host's subordinating words;
   pairwise relations; occupations; held sites; the host's satellites at their frozen site points; its lineage claims
   while that lane is lit; banded culture distances; the lit water lanes; the road watches; the DM's christenings. On a
   standalone world: the recipe's seats at their tiers, the middle prosperity rung, every pair neutral, links and
   relations only where the recipe gives them. No budget, cost vector or power key is ever asked of the host.
6. **Travel time, culture and water.** For each projecting seat s, one bounded Dijkstra over the fine raster from its
   cell under the cost law's time terms at the travel law's foot pace, season-neutral (borders do not breathe with the
   seasons), stopped at the seat's cap: t(s, c) in integer minutes, a step across a reach ≥ `navigableM3s` adding
   `river.crossingDays` (the sway's own resistance, never a route time: a big river is a border). **Culture resists**
   (J382): on a host-bound world a step into cell c takes × (1 + φ × cd(s, home(c))), home(c) the W8a seat whose
   territory holds c and cd the host's own
   culture distance between the two seats, banded in fifths and sent with the polity facts — a pair the host did not
   send reads 0, reported once per window (`W_POLITY_CULTURE_ABSENT`), and while an occupation stands on a seat the band
   between that seat and every seat of its occupier's allegiance is held at its value in the occupation's first window
   (held because an occupation may move its governance and alignment terms while no holder changes, (12); whether its
   governance term reads a shared sovereign or only a government label is H25's question); the map
   invents no culture measure, and on a standalone world cd is 0. **Water carries cheaply only along the host's lit
   water lanes** (J382):
   open water and lakes are a barrier to the sway, except that while the host's lane system is lit a seat at one end of
   an adopted lane reaches the other end at the travel law's water price; a reach that lands across water holds at most
   a **coastal lodgement** — the land within `lodgementDays` of its landing — never the far shore beyond. No water cell is
   ever held.
7. **Strength and reach (T2: "bounded but exponential").** L(s, c) = Λ − t(s, c) ÷ τ(s), with τ(s) = τTier[tier] ×
   kSize[size third] × kProsperity[r(s)] × (1 + B(s)), B the chain bonus of (9) and τTier = `reachTierDays` ÷ Λ. The
   size third counts the seat's own people only: a satellite projects itself ((12)) and is never counted in its
   parent's size (J384 (11)). **Prosperity is relative** (J384 (1)): r(s) is the seat's rung minus the realm's median
   rung (the realm here the campaign's seats on this world, never the `realm` size rung), clamped to ±`prosperityClamp`
   — the median the lower median of every projecting seat's rung (satellites, which send none, excluded), **held**: it moves
   only when a new value has stood `prosperityDwellWeeks`, and its move is one whole-world revision ((13)) recorded as
   `SwayRevision.medianRung`; on a standalone world every seat reads 0. τTier rises by rung by a factor of at least 1.5,
   kSize by 1.15 per third and kProsperity by 1.1 per relative rung (V13 §2.3's cells), so ln τ — and with it the log
   of a settlement's reach, where L falls to the floor 0, Λ·τ(s) — rises by at least ln 1.5 per tier rung and linearly
   in the size third and the relative rung: the reach grows at least exponentially with tier, size and prosperity, and
   it is bounded: reach(s) = min(Λ·τ(s), capTier[tier]).
   Every comparison is linear in t, in fixed-point
   thousandths; no exponential is evaluated. A cell no seat reaches is **unclaimed** and stays wild: the map never fills
   it.
8. **Neighbours (T2: "dynamics of neighbors").** Per cell the candidates are grouped by allegiance (9); an allegiance
   scores the greatest L of its members. The top two (ties by the root's key) are compared by the class of the **local
   pair** — never their roots' — read through the adapter folder's class table over the host's relationship-state
   labels (the plane its simulation reads): **kin** (one allegiance); **respect** (alliance and patron–client, a
   compelled ally — a live compelled-alliance term — and a pair under a live mutual-defence term, J397 (M13)); **neutral**
   (neutral, trade partnership and criminal network, no relation, and a pair under a live non-aggression term whatever
   its relationship label, J397 (M13) — the host's `PolityRelation.terms` read first, its label second: a sworn peace
   draws no debatable land, no push and no doubled patrols between the two); **adversarial** (rivalry, cold war, hostility and
   the legacy *tense*, and any pair at war — a pair at war under a non-aggression term is at war); a term the host sends
   unenforced (`terms[].enforced` absent or false) still sets the class, the legend noting on the pair "sworn, not yet
   kept by the host's law" (V13 §5.1), so the promise is drawn and said to be a promise; the vassal
   labels are member links (9), never a class. Kin and respect split at the travel-time
   midline, each within its own reach, and never push; neutral: the stronger holds; **adversarial: the push is the
   host's** (J384 (3)) — at a cell both reach (each with L > 0), the two local seats are compared on travel time alone
   at the steeper fade, P(x, c) = Λ − t(x, c) ÷ τmin + `margins.pushPerBand` × the host's strength band of x
   (`PolitySeat.strengthBand`), τmin the smaller of the two τ; the side whose lead in P is at least `margins.civ` holds,
   else the cell is **debatable** — the contested march, held by neither — unless (10) decides it; a cell only one of
   them reaches is that one's. So the map's projection keeps each side's reach, floor and ceiling, and the host's own
   strength order — the comparator its relationship drift reads to choose a raider and an overlord — decides which way
   the line is pushed: two systems never decide one contest, and the map's vassal reinforcement ((9)) stays out of the
   push. A strength band counts once it has stood `margins.strengthDwellWeeks`, the pair reading until then the last
   band it counted, level if none; while the host sends none for a pair, the pair reads level (no push), reported once
   per window (`W_POLITY_STRENGTH_ABSENT`). A third allegiance never holds a cell where it ranks third; the clerk names
   it **outranked** (never *claimant*, the host's word for an heir). **The seat
   rule:** a seat's own cell and a placed frame's extent are always held by their seat; only an occupation marks them.
9. **The continuous chain of vassals (T2).** **The host's membership walk first** (J400 (6)): where the polity window carries the host's walk (`PolityFacts.walk`, V13 §2.2), the allegiance graph IS the walk — each seat's root, liege, tier and class as the host's one membership read gives them, its `basis` read through the adapter folder's link table as a link's word is, so a tributary, a compelled ally and an occupation short of vassalage are drawn as this rule and (12) draw them — and the map never derives a kingdom the host derives; a covert membership of the walk is drawn only on the DM's picture, as a covert link is (T-V13-41 (j)), and a seat the walk omits reads its raw links, never rooting itself by omission; the raw links stay, read for the DM's diagnostic (`whyCell` and the clerk name the links beside the walk) and as the arm where no walk is sent; every drawing rule below — the chain's depth, continuity in two passes, exclaves, the chain bonus and the reinforcement — applies over the walk's membership exactly as over the links'. Where no walk is sent, the allegiance graph is built from the host's links: members are the seats
   the host subordinates as a polity — a vassal (its relationship-state plane's vassal labels), an occupation at its
   vassalized rung, a puppet seat. A **tributary** is a seat bound to another by a live tribute term (one of the host's
   four subordinating treaty terms), never by a relation label: it keeps its own sway outside the allegiance, drawn with
   its overlord's band; a compelled ally is respect (8); an occupation short of vassalage, a treaty-held one included, is
   an overlay (12); a satellite of the host projects inside its parent's allegiance as a claim point (12) but is never a chain member (no
   bonus, no continuity test). The host's
   own subordination set (tribute, compelled alliance, puppet seat, a treaty-held occupation) is so drawn three ways —
   member, band and relation, overlay — a divergence J-V13.67 records. The root is a seat with no member link upward; a
   cycle drops the later link (`W_POLITY_CYCLE`); a seat with two lieges ranks vassalized, vassal, puppet, then the
   earlier link, the other drawn as a claim (`W_POLITY_TWO_LIEGES`). **Continuity in two passes, never iterated.** Pass 1
   runs (7)–(8) with every chain bonus B = 0 and no reinforcement: a member is **continuous** when the host's own reach
   verdict for the link says so, else when its bonus-free sway shares a border with its overlord's or a continuous
   member's bonus-free sway, or a road the host does not grade hidden joins its seat to that sway within Treinf — the
   host's reinforcement band from the travel law, in cost units under the calibration sent with it (V13 §2.3), never
   authored here; otherwise it is an **exclave**: a member, drawn detached, with no reinforcement and no bonus. Pass 2
   applies the bonus and the reinforcement to the members pass 1 found continuous; its result is final. With T(a, b) the
   seat-to-seat cost under the cost law (Treinf's units), the chain bonus B(o) = min(`bMax`, Σ over o's continuous
   members m of wTier[m] × δ^(depth−1) × max(0, 1 − T(o, m) ÷ Treinf)), depth ≤ `depthMax`, each tributary of o, though
   outside the allegiance, counting in B at × `wTributary`; B grows the overlord's own reach and never passes its cap;
   each continuous member's τ takes (1 + B(root) × δ^depth); a continuous member's reinforcement — its root's
   ρ × δ^(depth−1) × max(0, 1 − T(root, v) ÷ Treinf) — is read only by (10)'s military tie-break inside debatable
