| `setRequirements`, `decide` | a Re-derive from the earliest stage a changed row affects (`PresetRule.options[].stage`), over the whole extent or the row's region | every lock; every override; every placement; every disturbance | declared from that stage |
| `regenerate` of `stage: 'formation'` | a new scenario draw, a new bake, Re-derive from W1 | every override and disturbance (held, kept); placements (re-blended or marked stale as a `worldRecipe` op's row says) | declared whole-world (+ `formationMs`) |

**Edit fates** (§7.3's `EditFate`) on a world re-derivation: a placement is `kept`; a proposal inside a changed
watershed `discarded`; a reach `carried` by its anchor or `orphaned` (its name kept on the tombstone for V11's reuse); a
territory `reshaped` with the cells moved; a dated surface `kept`. **Recorded inputs** of the world are its recipe,
its seats and every placement; of a frame its charter.

### 4.4 Undo

Every event's undo is V13 §1b.3's row: the replaced scope (for a re-derivation) or the inverse (for an attribute).
A placement edit's undo restores the former placement, its blend (the trace re-applied) and its charter copy, and emits
in the frame's log the inverse `charter` event (the former `worldRef` and `Recipe.charter`); the derived readings
(datum, wind, sun) follow the world; a `worldWins` undo is the frame's Re-derive from S1 undo (the base's: the replaced
scope restored byte-identical). A `happened` edit's undo removes its dated surface and traces together (the group);
`deleteTrace`'s undo restores the trace alone; a `carrySurface`'s undo removes the frame's carried surface and its
traces with the world's edit as one pair (the frame's `setSurface` authored `world` sits in no user's undo stack of
the frame, as the `charter` event does; V13 §3.11.5 (3); J397 (M32); BCR-V13-54). The world and the frame have separate logs and separate undo stacks
(§7.4's per-document sessions): a placement edit is one group in the world's log; its fold writes the frame through
the frame's own `charter` event (author `world`, the reserved session `world:place` — §7.4's second reserved session
beside `host:port`, BCR-V13-9 — with no group, so it sits in no user's undo stack; C13-40), and the world's undo record
holds the pair (the world event, the frame event's `seq`) so the two are undone together and a bridged client of the
frame (§11.3) sees the change as an ordinary log event. The frame's user cannot undo the world's placement from the
frame; `unplaceFrame` on the world is the way. **One history, two logs** (J397 (M39)): the world page's campaign
history view (`CampaignTimeline`, V13 §2.4; V09 §4.22 (11)) lists the world's and its placed frames' dated events on
one timeline — edits by their week, host events, disturbances, dated surfaces, placements and windows, each entry
opening its own document at that entry — read from the world's log, its event index and each frame's log through
`worldRef`, audience-filtered as a lens is; it is a reading and never a third undo stack: undo stays per document,
and an entry's undo is that document's own, taken on that document's page. On a host-bound world a host input (a window, a seat binding, the
genesis, the laws) is never a user's undo target — the host's own undo arrives as a later window that retracts — and a
world edit the host has `consumed` is sealed: its undo is refused and its reversal is a new edit offered to the host.
T-V13-27 replays every edit kind forward and back.

### 4.5 The counterfactual fork

`fork` copies the document's current state into a fork (the base's Preview-on-a-copy, T10; the fork is a `Document`
with `forkOf: { doc; seq }` and no canonical log position); edits on the fork fold as usual, the cascade runs on it,
the view shows it (with the diff layer: changed units by class, moved reaches, flooded faces against the canonical
state); `commitFork` replays the fork's events onto the canonical log under the given verb as one group (each event
re-folded at its new log position — the fork's results are never copied; a conflict with an event committed since the
fork's `seq` is F-EDIT's outcome per event); `discardFork` drops it. Forks never persist in the canonical document
(a reload drops them; V13 §2.6's row). `forkAt(h, seq)` (§11.2) is the clerk's `whatIf` entry (V13 §4.7), the week mapped to the `seq` of the last event at
or before that week: a fork whose surfaces are those in force at `week` and whose cascade runs from there. A fork of a
host-bound world neither sends nor receives a port message; its preview shows `timeDelta` against the adopted canon.
**A baked step on a fork** (J-V13.111): a `physicsPass` of depth `weather` bakes its `weather` op once on the fork (the
op's payload chunks written to the fork's `fields`), and `commitFork` carries the op WITH its bake onto the canonical
log — the one kind of event whose fold reads a recorded result instead of re-running (as W1 reads every baked op), so
"the fork's results are never copied" holds for every re-derivable step, and the bake, which is never re-derivable
by design, rides the event as the `image` op's asset rides its op. **Every physics pass** runs through this
preview-and-commit: the diff layer shows the cells changed by layer, the overrides released, the sailing legs and
band crossings moved (the crossings as one line of the diff summary, the warning itself raised at the commit, J397
(M40)) and the conflicts raised (V13 §3.11.5 (1)); the DM commits under the verb the depth implies —
`rederive` and `release` as `alwaysSo` (the physics was always so), `weather` — "Weather (geological years)", its
years the land's and never the campaign's (J397 (M36)) — as `happened` at the fork's week (a
span of time passed, its former ground a `TerrainTrace`) — or discards.

### 4.6 Loading older documents

A frame saved before this volume loads with: `Terrain.surfaces` built from its water bodies (one surface per body
from `seaLevelCm`, the spill heights and the carved bed), `carveDeltaCm` empty and reported (`W_MIGRATE_NO_CARVE`:
`preCarveHeightAt` equals `heightAt` and bar 5's re-route reads the carved bed until a Re-derive from S1 re-makes the
delta), `Terrain.groundwater` derived on load from the surfaces (reported as the version's shift: cellar classes may
change — the base's migration rule shows the diff, §7.4), `EditBase.verb` read as `alwaysSo` on every older event,
`Document.worldRef` absent (standalone), `Recipe.charter` absent. The world document has no older form. The
migration is one `migration`-authored event group at the log's end (the base's rule), undoable as a group.

### 4.7 The clerk's view: reason records and the four readers

Every stage and every cascade step writes a `ReasonRecord` — the one declaration of V13 §2.2 (C13-07) — per record
and per raster chunk; a cell's reason is `whyCell(raster, cell)`, computed on demand from the chunk's record. The
readers in `@plat/world/why`, exposed through V10's `why` query (V10 §3.9) by a new field `ask` beside the existing
`mode: 'asPlaced'|'asNow'`, which the readers pass through to the kind's provider (BCR-V13-24; C13-39):

| reader | question | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `why(fact)` | "why is this so" | the fact's latest reason rendered (the `MsgRef` with its numbers: "flooded because the floor sits 212 cm below a table set by the river's surface 40 m away, reached through the collapsed passage"); the rule row named; the inputs listed as links |
| `whatCaused(fact)` | "what made this happen" | the chain: the fact's reason → each input's reason, depth-first to the recorded inputs (a recipe op, a placement, an edit event, a table cell), rendered as a tree with the event dates; a missing link is named ("the chain is incomplete at the sewer outfall: derived before this version"); where an input is a host event (a `WorldEvent` holding `causedBy`) the chain descends ONE level into the host's receipt ids, each rendered as the host's — its kind, its week, its seat, named as the host's and opened on the host's own surface by the headline join (V13 §3.11.6; J397 (M7), (M11)) — the map re-reading no host law and rendering no receipt's content; `reasonOf` (V13 §3.11.6) is this reader flattened in walk order — it returns the chain rendered for the asking audience, a sentence and a week per hop — for the host's cause walk (H43), so one "why" walks from the drought to the hunger across the seam, each half in its own voice |
| `whatChanged(fact, since)` | "what changed here since week w" | every reason with `supersedes` written after `since` whose fact is the asked one or an input of it, with the event and verb ("the ford is gone because the river was re-routed in year 412, this happened") |
| `whatIf(edit)` | "what if …" | `forkAt` + the edit's dry run on the fork + the cascade's change list rendered: counts by consumer kind, the three largest changes named, the coherence cost for a placement |

The clerk's placement proposal (`placeAt`, V10 §3.9's proposal form) is `nearestLawful` rendered as a proposal the user
accepts (`proposedBy: 'clerk'`). A reason's `text` is a `MsgRef` (§5.4's form) so every rendering is per caller and
never carries a withheld name (V10's visibility rule applies: a reason whose input the viewer may not see renders the
input as "something you cannot see"). Reason records sit outside the model digest and inside the records digest (V13
§2.7); a fact without one fails T-V13-10.

## 5 Rendering, labels and exports

### 5.1 The world map: layers and styles (§8's pipeline, the world's rows; BCR-V13-13)

The world document renders through the base's tile pipeline (§8.1) with its own layer set, declared as `LayerSpec`
rows of the `world` product (C13-60 (e)) (the view's `worldLayer` key picks the thematic layer; the structural layers always draw):

| layer | kind | draws | style row (§8.3's style table, the world's rows in `@plat/tables` `style.world`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `relief` (default thematic) | raster | the DEM as hypsometric tint × hillshade (the sun from §8.4's path sun at the world's default week and hour; the shade is the base's light pass at the vector rung — no light tiles at world scale, §8.4) | eight tint bands by elevation (our own ramp: shore green → upland ochre → alpine grey → ice white; the bands' bounds in metres as cells of the row) |
| `biome` | raster | `biome` per fine cell — the potential natural vegetation (W5), named so in the legend; never the land cover | one fill per `BiomeRow` (the row's `colour` cell, own palette) |
| `climate` | raster | `tempDeciC` or `precipMm` (a sub-key) | two diverging ramps |
| `monthly` | raster | `tempMonthDeciC[m]`, `precipMonthMm[m]` or the month's wind (a month sub-key on a month slider) | the climate ramps; the wind as a sparse arrow field |
| `currents` | vector | `currentMonth[m]` on ocean cells as a sparse arrow field, `sstAnomalyDeciC` as a warm–cold tint along the coasts (a month sub-key) | the sea's blue family; a warm red and a cold blue tint |
| `soil` | raster | `soil` per formation cell with the fine-scale overrides applied at draw (V13 §3.2.1 (9)) | one fill per `SoilRule` row (the row's `colour`) |
| `bedrock` | raster | `bedrock` per formation cell | a categorical palette (own) |
| `landforms` | vector | every `Landform`'s outline and crest; an `active` volcano's mark | 0.8 px outline, the crest 1.2 px; the volcano glyph |
| `landCover` | raster | the cover plate's class per fine cell at `lensWeek` (V13 §3.6 (5)) — a derived world layer, NOT a lens: audience-filtered as a lens's marks are (V13 §5.8 (9)), its legend's first row "derived land cover: the map's own derivation from the campaign's dated facts; the host's dossier holds the biome", a cell's hover naming its class, its last event and the weeks since (a withdrawn field "withdrawn week n: beyond the town's demand since", its succession from that week; J397 (M26)); drawn in two forms — as the thematic fill under `worldLayer: 'landCover'` (every class filled), and, in the DEFAULT picture under `relief`, as an **overlay** of the used and disturbed classes alone over the relief (fields, pasture, coppice, fallow, scrub, regrowth and scars at the plate's week; a cell at its potential vegetation's own class left to the relief), so the world page shows its fields and scars by default (J394; the `atlas` layer set of V13 §5.4 reads this form) | one fill per `world.cover` class (own palette: fields ochre, pasture pale green, coppice dark green, fallow buff, scars grey, silt brown, ash pale grey, lava black); the overlay at 70 % alpha |
| `watershed` | raster | `watershed` by id | a hashed categorical palette (`H32` of the id, no table; C13-44) |
| `waterTable` | raster | `tableCm − dem` depth bands | a six-band ramp (0–0.5, 0.5–1, 1–2, 2–5, 5–10, > 10 m) |
| `water` | vector | seas and lakes as polygons at their surface (the coast outline from W2 at the stop's tolerance); reaches as polylines with the width from the stage profile, drawn only when ≥ `style.world`'s `riverDrawM3s[stop]` cells (stop 0: 60, 1: 20, 2: 5, 3: 2 m³/s; own, calibratable, registered in the style table — C13-31) | the base's water style rows (the same blue family; §8.3) |
| `traces` (under `showTraces`) | vector | `oldShore` as a dashed line, `oldBed` as a hatched band, `oldGround` as a stippled fill; a `SurfaceTrace` as a dotted level line; an `Override`'s cells as a hatch in its layer's colour (a released one dotted); a released override kept as history by its former value's outline | the base's "former" style (the dashed grey of V06's history frames) |
| `routes` | vector | `WorldRoute` by class, or by the host's grade on a host-bound world, at the network in force at the view's week; a hidden host road a DM-only ghost, a hidden water lane a quiet-quay mark; lengths labelled in km, and — on a host-bound world — the host's own travel time where it sends one: a leg's frozen weeks (`TravelLaw.legWeeks`) or the weeks its own law gives under the calibration it sent (`derivedTime` with the law's `basis`), labelled with the basis word the host sends (`TravelLaw.calibration.basisWord`: "by the host's law — normalized: relative to this realm's nearest-neighbour hop", or its metric word), never a map-derived time there and never the default row's (J397 (M5): two clocks, one the host's, each named); on a standalone world no time, or `derivedTime` labelled with the law and "on foot"; at a crossing whose toll holder differs from the sway's holder the hover "tolls to {seat}" (V13 §3.9 (16); J397 (M18); no soak: the gate stays the toll holder's and the host reads none of the map feed's holders, J400 (12)); every time on this layer is a route's LABEL in weeks — information, never a journey the map runs for the party: no path is drawn from the party pin, no arrival is computed and no day is counted (J399 (R4), (R5); the `partyPin` row) | highway 2 px solid, road 1.2 px, track 0.8 px dashed, trail 0.5 px dotted, sea 1 px dashed blue, river (navigable) a darker water line |
| `seatTerritory` (thematic, diagnostic) | vector | W8a's seat territories, borders 0.6 px, and the crossings as small ticks | hashed categorical palette |
| `sway` (with `allegianceBorder`, `memberBorder`) | vector | W8b at the revision in force at the view's `lensWeek` (the document's week unless the scrub sets it): fills at 18 % alpha in the allegiance's colour (`H32` of the root's key, or the host's colour when sent; stable while the root holds), unclaimed land unfilled; allegiance borders 2 px solid; member borders 0.8 px between member sways (stop ≥ 1); an exclave its own outer border with a 1 px dotted halo; satellites dots only, at their frozen site points; a tributary its own fill with its border doubled by an inner 1.5 px band in its overlord's colour; claims DM-only as outlines of the target's sway in the claimant's colour — a lineage claim (a sale's, and the host's own while its lineage lane is lit) dashed, a vengeance licence dot-dashed, a sold town's grievance dotted (J397 (M20); `PolityFacts.claims[].kind`), each fading at its lapse week; razed land scorched (`swayStatus` 4): unfilled, a scorched hatch in neutral ink for its dwell, the legend "razed: unclaimed until the ash cools" (J397 (M14)); the legend's label the DM's christening, else the root's descriptive label — the host sends no name of its own (V13 §3.9 (17); J400 (2)); a treaty the host does not yet enforce noted on its pair "sworn, not yet kept by the host's law" (J397 (M13)); a pact of the realm's past standing at week 0 noted on its pair "sworn n years before the campaign" (`PolityRelation.terms[].pastFact`) and a tie or relation so standing "since n years before the campaign" (`sincePast`), never "since week 0" (J400 (14)); standalone provinces at stop ≥ 2 as 0.6 px dashed; at a `lensWeek` before the live campaign's `fromWeek` (V13 §2.2's `CampaignRecord`) the revision in force THEN — the earlier campaign's sway, drawn only there, in history, under the label "before this campaign: {name}, its year n" (J399 (R1); V13 §5.8 (8)) — and, between a binding and the new campaign's birth window, no live sway (the legend: "awaiting this campaign's first window") | the allegiance palette |
| `occupation`, `debatable`, `fighting` | vector | occupation: a diagonal hatch in the occupier's colour over the occupied sway, dense to light by the host's rung (neutral ink when the occupier is unrecorded); debatable: a cross-hatch in the two sides' colours, no fill; held by force: the holder's fill with a single hatch in the other side's colour; fighting: a crossed-blades mark at each open engagement and a 2 px edge on its segment — no arrows, no animation; a fought-over wild (V13 §3.9 (11); J397 (M19)): the crossed blades at the seats' midpoint in wild land with its band and the label "fought-over wild", no segment; the legend owning both "contested"s — "contested: the host's occupation at its first rung; debatable: the map's debatable land between adversaries" (J397 (M21)) — and reading "raids move no line; the host's strength band may" beside the fighting mark (J397 (M16)) | the sides' colours |
| `patrols` (a toggle) | vector | `PatrolCadence` per route segment at the revision in force at the view's `lensWeek`: tinted by cadence (weekly, monthly, seasonal), both colours striped on a debatable segment, no arrows or headings; a covert power's DM-only; its legend's first row "the map's patrols: a picture of who could watch these roads — the host gives it no meaning" (J400 (18)); the host's own patrols, where the host lights them, as dated pins at their place and week, "the host's patrol, week n" (a host patrol, V13 §5.9 (3)), never a tint | the powers' colours |
| `events` (with a "this advance" filter — the map's half of the host's session-prep letter, J397 (M11): the last window's dated events, each with its headline where the host holds one) | pins | `WorldEvent`s by kind at their place up to the view's `lensWeek`, a glyph's lifecycle mark at once (razed, besieged, occupied), DM-only docket pins; a pending sway trigger as a planting line until it takes effect or lapses (V13 §3.9 (13)); every `Disturbance` at its week by its kind's glyph over its cells; the host's knowledge events (a plant, an intercept, a burned agent: a `kind` the adapter folder's event table marks `knowledge`) as DM-only dated pins where sent, never a player's; a pin's card carries the action **open the headline** where the event holds `causedBy` receipts and the host registers `headlineOf` (V13 §3.11.6) — drawn by V09 as the lens-mark card is (BCR-V13-39), the card's own words V13's — and, DM-only, the host's integrity register word where sent (`WorldEvent.integrity`: clean, worn in the telling, planted); on a player's picture a public pin draws at its week, or, under the default-preset arm, when the news reaches the party (V13 §5.8 (7); J397 (M10)); a pin of an earlier campaign (its week before the live campaign's `fromWeek`) draws under "before this campaign: {name}, its year n" and opens read-only (J399 (R1); V13 §5.2); at a scrub position inside **the realm's past** (its strip ahead of the world clock, V13 §5.8 (8)), the host's past facts (`PastFacts`) of that year as pins at their seats — a fact of a pair a pin at each of its two seats naming the other, never a line —, each "{n} years before the campaign" with the host's sentence, PENCILLED (a dashed pin; the legend "pencilled: the realm's past as the host offers it, inked at the first advance") until the first advance inks it, then inked, DM-only unless the host resolves a fact public; nothing else drawn live there — no sway, border, route or lens mark: the realm's past has no geometry, and the ground under it is the world as it is, the legend saying so (J400 (21)) | the notice style |
| `lens:<id>` (under `worldLens`, one per open lens) | vector and pins | V13 §5.9's elements at `lensWeek`, the regime banner first in the legend | `style.world`'s lens rows, one per element key (V11 writes them) |
| `settlements` | vector | every `Glyph` at the stop's level (V13 §5.2): a frame's `SettlementGlyph`; a site's drawn at level 0 by its `glyph` mark's `class` icon at the pin size (SW-08) | the glyph style rows (dot by tier size: 3–9 px; ring 1 px; outline fill at 60 % of the built colour; water, wall and way in the base's colours at world weight) |
| `resources`, `springs`, `proposals` | pins | W5's resources, W4's springs, W6's proposals (while shown) | the base's pin style, one icon kind per resource (own glyphs) |
| `placements` | vector | the placed frames' outlines (the arena's outer ring through `toWorld`) and the blend band's outline on hover | 1 px accent; the band dotted |
| `anomalies` | pins | `PlacementAnomaly` | the notice style |
| `partyPin` | pins | the party's place (J399 (R4); J400 (9); V13 §2.2's `PartyPlacement` and `LensFacts.partySeats`): its CURRENT place as the party glyph — on a standalone world the pin's latest placement, "the party is here" and its week; on a host-bound world ALWAYS the host's whereabouts of the party (one seat: the glyph at the seat; a pair: the glyph at each of its two seats captioned "between {A} and {B}", never a line between them; "the party is at {seat}" where the host holds the DM's present-at, "last heard at {seat}, week n" where it holds the last heard) — a map-only placement off every host-bound settlement (or back-dated) later than the host's `partyStamp` drawn BESIDE it as a narration mark of its own (the notice style, never the party glyph), "where the game master narrates them, week n", and a present-at placement drawn PENDING (a hollow glyph, on the DM's picture alone; the legend "sent to the host; shown once its next advance carries it", `W_PARTY_PENDING`) until the host's next window carries it (then the host's glyph) or names other seats (the glyph at the host's place: the host is the writer); where the host sends no whereabouts no party glyph is drawn and every placement is a narration mark —, for every audience its `audience` admits (a party's picture draws its current public place and nothing older); under the DM-only `showPinHistory` key the earlier placements as dated dots, each with its week and note — never a line, arrow or path between any two (the host's ambiguity law for movers, V13 §5.8 (5), kept for the party itself), never an ETA, never a day count; a placement at a seat sits on the glyph; in the VTT scene the current place is a note and a later narration mark a second note, a pending placement on the DM's scene alone (V13 §5.4); never in `renderAt`'s `atlas` set (a mark of the page, not of the member's picture, V13 §5.4) | the notice style; the party glyph (own) |
| `labels` | the base's label layer | V13 §5.3 | §9's |

**The player picture** (J-V13.77): a player audience sees the sway re-derived at the head revision over the host's
whitelisted political facts — covert links, their exclaves and covert patrols omitted as entities, never greyed — or,
when the host sends `audienceKnowledge`, over the facts that audience knows (an unknown later fact absent, never
guessed), cached per (revision, known set); the player picture reads force, strength and culture bands only where the host's
whitelist admits them (absent, a debatable cell stays debatable unless a fight verdict the audience is shown decides it,
V13 §3.9 (11), an adversarial pair reads level and culture reads 0, and
its relative rungs read against the median of the rungs it is shown: fail-closed, J-V13.77); under an
omniscient regime (no belief recorded) the picture is the sway over the host's public facts — and, where the host sends
the party's whereabouts, over the public facts the party has heard of: a public political fact or event enters the party's
known set `partyNewsDelay` weeks after its week (the default-preset arm, V13 §5.8 (7); J397 (M10)), the map deriving
the known subset `audienceKnowledge` would carry where the host sends none (the host's set wins where it does), so a
border three weeks' ride away moves on the party's map when the news could have reached it, never before; where the
host records belief and sends the party observer's court's believed political facts, the party's sway is that
court's believed sway — the court viewpoint of V13 §5.9 (2) drawn for the party, captioned "as {court} believes it,
as of week n" — and else the known truth as above (J397 (M9)); the DM always sees the
head revision. The layers above are the first rows of the lens mechanism (V13 §5.8): `seatTerritory`, `sway`,
`occupation`, `debatable` and `fighting` are the sway lens (the owner's territory rules) and `patrols` the patrols lens
(V13 §5.9), their scrub the sway's revision history; every other lens draws under its own layer key (`lens:<id>`), toggled by the view key
`worldLens`.

The world draws on the base's integer-cm viewport (§8.1) with the world's cm as the arena coordinate — the view's
transform is the same code with a larger extent; the tile cache is keyed by the world document's digest as a frame's
is. On the **frame** document this volume adds three overlays (`waterClass`: units tinted by class — dry none, damp a
hatched blue, wading light blue, swimming blue, submerged dark blue with a ghosted outline; `flood`: the spread at the
chosen stage with depth bands and the barrier edges that stopped it; `traces` as above) and the **waterline** on walls
(a building's elevation render draws a line at the governing surface's height on every storey the stage reaches), the
submerged ruin as a ghost at depth < `style.world.ghostDepthCm` (300) and withheld deeper (below the viewer's key, V10's
visibility), and the encounter crop reads `classifyWater` for every face of its resolved set and `routeClass` over its
ways (V14's E3 (7)); the crop's water rendering is V14 §5.3's (SW-18).

### 5.2 Zoom stops, the glyph levels and opening a settlement

The world band has four stops (`worldZoom` 0–3; the view's zoom is continuous and the stop is the floor): stop 0
shows the whole extent (a continent at ~0.25 px per fine cell), stop 1 is 4 ×, stop 2 is 16 ×, stop 3 is 64 × (a
fine cell at 16 px: the finest the world draws — beyond it the frame opens). At each stop every glyph draws its
`GlyphLevelRow` by V13 §2.3's rule (the highest level whose stop range holds the stop, whose `minTier` the tier
meets and whose `fromStopByTier` for the tier is ≤ the stop: a THORP or HAMLET draws from stop 2 only; C13-52). **Opening the settlement:** a click on a glyph at any stop (or the
`open` action on the placement card) opens the frame document as another page (V09's document router: a new page with
the frame's own view, the world page kept in its tab; the back action returns to the world at the same stop and
centre) — the owner's correction (2): the world map shows the generalization, the full settlement is another page,
never an in-place zoom into the arena. A stale glyph (`sourceDigest` ≠ the frame's) is re-made before it draws when the
frame is open in the same host, else drawn as is with a stale mark. A hover shows the placement card (name, tier,
population, the stamp, the coherence cost by term, anomalies, `open`, `worldWins` when stale) — its DM-facing words
V09 §4.22 (11)'s (J397 (M34): the cost as "how it fits the land", the stamp as "the land yields to the town" or "the
town was placed on the land", each anomaly a sentence, `worldWins` as "Re-make the town from the land", stale as
"the land under this town has changed"; this volume owns the facts, V09 the words). The world page also offers the
**campaign history** view (V13 §4.4; V09 §4.22 (11); J397 (M39)): one timeline of the world's and its towns' dated
events, each entry opening its document; on a sequel world (J399 (R1); V13 §2.2's `CampaignRecord`) the timeline runs
back through every earlier campaign's weeks on the world clock, each earlier entry under "before this campaign: {name},
its year n" (`CampaignTimeline.entries[].campaign`, V13 §2.4) and READ-ONLY — it opens its document with the scrub at
that week and no edit offered: a closed campaign's weeks admit no edit (`refuse.world.campaignClosed`) and the world's
undo never reaches below the live campaign's `fromWeek` (V13 §4.1) —, and the gap between two campaigns is one entry,
"{n} years pass — between {A} and {B}", with nothing in it but the cover's recovery (V13 §5.8 (9)). **The realm's past** heads the timeline where the host sends it (J400 (21); V13 §2.2's `PastFacts`; `CampaignTimeline.past`, V13 §2.4): one group per campaign whose host sent a past, in the campaigns' order, each counted back from its campaign's first week (on a sequel world headed "the realm's past, as {name} began" and adding "the host's history as {name} began — it may tell of years when {earlier} was played here"), each fact an entry in years — "{n} years before the campaign — {seat, or the two seats}: {the host's sentence}" —, pencilled or inked as the host holds it, read-only and opening nothing (it has no document and no week), never interleaved with any campaign's weeks: an earlier campaign is play on this world, the realm's past the host's history before a campaign (law (9) of V13 §3.11.6).

### 5.3 Labels

W9's candidates (V13 §3.10 (2)) run through §9's placer per stop with `world.labels`'s rows: priority by kind (the
settlement's × tier), the zoom extent per kind, `spreadPx` 12 as the collision margin, a river label along its course
only when the reach's length ≥ `riverMinKm` 30 (shorter rivers unlabelled at every stop), a sea's label at its pole of
inaccessibility at the stop's largest size, a landform's along its crest (a range, a rift, an arc) or at its outline's
pole (a volcano, a fjord, a glacial lake, a plateau) under the `range` kind's priority and zoom extent (V13 §3.10
(2)), an allegiance's at its root sway's `poleCm` in small capitals (the DM's christening, else a descriptive label from its root's name; never a W9 name on a host-bound world), a standalone province's at stop ≥ 2.
The placer's ladder is §9.4's (F-LABEL: view data, never a model change); label positions are cached per (document
digest, stop). A settlement's label is its name beside the dot (stop 0–1) or under the outline (stop 2–3), the tier
by the base's type scale.

### 5.4 Exports (§11.1's pipeline; the world's exporters in `@plat/export`; BCR-V13-12)

| export | shape | contents | source of the shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ecosystemJson` | the reference ecosystem's full-map JSON (version-pinned to the adapter folder) | the cell graph re-expressed from the fine raster (one cell per `exportStride` fine cells, the size row's: 10 at the continent rung, 7 at the realm, 4 at the province — ≤ 100 k cells, the range the ecosystem's tools were built for; the dialog shows the count and admits another stride; C13-57), heights on the reference's scale by the schema's inverse law, biomes by the schema's mapping, rivers from the reaches, lakes, settlements from the settlement map records (name, population, tier as the schema's size, port, capital), states from the allegiances (the schema file's neutral state for the unclaimed and debatable land), provinces from the member sways, zones for the debatable bands (the schema file's disputed kind) and the occupations, a diplomacy matrix only from the host's relations when sent (never invented), routes, cultures where the world has them, and the settings block's scale from the extent with the unit km and the scale in km per exported pixel (the inverse of the import's transform; the key names in the adapter folder's schema file) | `adapters/<ecosystem>/<version>/schema.json` (the key list and value laws; J-V13.46) — the exporter is written against the schema file, never against the reference's source |
| `ecosystemGeoJson` | GeoJSON FeatureCollection with the reference ecosystem's property names | cells (Polygon, on request, with `soil` and `bedrock` as properties), rivers (LineString with discharge, width, name), lakes (Polygon), settlements (Point with name, population, port, capital, `tier`, and `placement` properties: origin, bearing, mirrored, stamp), allegiances and member sways (MultiPolygon with `status`, `allegiance` and `swayRevision`), routes (LineString with class or grade; a water route's `sailing` efforts per vessel, month and direction as properties, its differing courses as further LineStrings on request), landforms (LineString crest and Polygon outline with `kind`, `name`, `heightM`, `active`), springs (Point), traces (kind `trace`), overrides and disturbances (kind `override` with its layer and value; kind `disturbance` with its kind, week and severity); never a cover plate (a derived layer at a week, not a model fact) | the same schema file's `geojson` block |
| `heightmap16` | a 16-bit PNG (and raw `.r16` on request) | the fine DEM mapped linearly from `minCm` to `maxCm` (both in the sidecar JSON with the extent, the cell size and the datum) — a standard-looking image for terrain tools | own |
| `worldCsv` | CSV, one file per kind in a zip | reaches (id, name, discharge, length, navigable, mouth), lakes, territories (the seat territories: id, name, area, seat), sways (id, seat, allegiance, status, revision), routes, sailing legs (route, vessel, month, direction, effort), landforms (id, kind, name, height), settlements (the map record's scalars, the cover shares at the export's week), proposals, resources, springs, the verification report's rows (requirement, status, by, reason) | own |
| the picture exports | the base's (§11.1: PNG/SVG/PDF of the view at a stop, the A2 300-dpi still) | the world view with its layers and labels | §11.1 unchanged; the world is one more document kind |
| **the world scene** (J399 (R3); BCR-V13-56; T-V13-123; `WORLD-24`) | one Foundry-class scene JSON and one Universal VTT file per world page, by §11.1's profile extended to the world rungs, written through V14 §5.3's shared writer `sceneSet` (one image and one JSON per scene; the `plat` object; the Foundry scene's `Level` per scene) | the world page at the chosen zoom stop (V13 §5.2's four) for the chosen audience: **the picture** — `renderAt(world, week, audience)`'s tiles at the stop (the rendered reading below: the member's default picture, every DM-only mark absent for a party or public audience, never greyed) with the `partyPin` layer's marks where the audience admits each — the party glyph at the party's current place (on a host-bound world the host's whereabouts), a later map-only placement a narration mark beside it, a pending placement on the DM's scene alone —, composed into the scene's background image at the stop's pixels (≤ 8 192 px a side; a larger picture a grid of scenes aligned to cells, §11.1's rule, the dialog showing it first); **the grid**, the DM's choice and presentation only — `grid: { kind: 'square'\|'hex'; kmPerCell: number } \| 'none'`: the cell an integer number of pixels (the dialog offers the km-per-cell values the stop's metres per pixel divide evenly, the one nearest 100 px first), a hex grid written as the Foundry scene's hex grid type and, in the Universal VTT file, as a square of the hex's width with `plat.grid.kind` `hex`, `none` as the Foundry scene's gridless type and the finest offered cell in the Universal VTT file with `plat.grid.kind` `none` — a cell carries no travel time and names no day (J399 (R5)): the tabletop's grid is the tabletop's, the map's times stay the routes' labels; **the notes** — every settlement glyph and site drawn at the stop as the scene's notes (the Foundry scene's `notes[]`, a journal page each; the Universal VTT file has none, so `plat.notes[]` carries them in the same form: the point in cells, the name, the kind) with their names and, for the DM audience alone, their reason sentences (`reasonOf`'s chain rendered, V13 §3.11.6), a party's or public note its name alone, and the party's current place a note in the `partyPin` layer's words ("the party is here", "last heard at {seat}, week n") and, on a host-bound world, a later map-only placement a second note in the narration's words ("where the game master narrates them, week n"), each where its audience admits it; **no walls, no lights** — `line_of_sight`, `objects_line_of_sight`, `portals` and `lights` empty, `environment.baked_lighting` true; **the `plat` object** — `plat.world { doc; rung; stop; audience; kmPerCell; gridKind }`, the date label and the season at the drawn week (§11.1's `season { week, name, winter }`), the world's digests and the output version (the provenance block's facts); **no player-writable layer** of ours (J399 (R6)) and nothing a player audience may not see (the audience's admission is §11.1's knowledge rule, through the picture and the notes alike) | `ExportOpts.vtt.world { stop; audience; grid; notes? }` (BCR-V13-56); the audience's admission as §11.1's knowledge rule; the file name `{world}-{stop}-{cols}x{rows}` (V09 §5.10) |

Every export's provenance block (§11.1) names the world's digests, the snapshot's versions and the export's schema
version; `ecosystemJson` export → the adapter's import → export is byte-identical over the schema's canonical form on
the shared keys (T-V13-26 (b): the round trip over the fixture, the keys V13 §3.15 names); the heightmap's round trip through the `image` op
reproduces the DEM within one cm per `minCm..maxCm` ÷ 65 535 (T-V13-28). The frame's exports gain `waterClass` on
every unit's record and the surfaces list (the base's JSON schema version bumps, §11.1's rule).

**The rendered reading** (`renderAt(world, week, audience)` → `RenderedWorld`, V13 §2.2; the spine's §14.2;
J-V13.127; file r item 1011; J-V13.134): the world's tiles at a week for an audience — the §8.1 tile sets at the four
stops over the **`atlas` layer set** — the member's DEFAULT PICTURE for that audience at the week (J394): V13 §5.1's
`relief` row with the cover plate's used and disturbed classes over it (the `landCover` row's overlay form at the
plate's week: fields, pasture, coppice, fallow, scrub, regrowth and scars; a cell at its potential vegetation's own
class left to the relief), `water`, `routes` (the network in force at the week), `settlements` with their glyphs at the
stop, `labels`, `sway` with its `allegianceBorder` and `memberBorder` at the revision in force, `occupation`,
`debatable`, `fighting`, and the `events` pins up to the week — each under the audience's admission (the player
picture of V13 §5.1 for a party, the cover layer's filter of V13 §5.8 (9); a DM-only mark never drawn for a player
audience) — and nothing else: no lens layer (an instrument a user toggles), no diagnostic layer (`placements`,
`anomalies`, `proposals`, `traces`, the `resources` and `springs` pins), no thematic fill other than `relief` (`biome`,
`climate`, `monthly`, `currents`, `soil`, `bedrock`), whatever the member's own view keys hold: a lens is a legended
instrument of a world page (V13 §5.8 (2)) and an atlas's picture carries no legend for it, while the sway, the events
and the land cover are the member's own dated facts at its present, which the picture already is (`opts.layers`
restricts the tiles to the `settlements` and `labels` rows alone, for V15 §3.5 (a); no other subset) — with the placed
label boxes per stop
(`RenderedWorld.tiles[].labels`, the placer's boxes at that stop in the member's pixel frame) — with the extent, the
datum, the latitude box, the rung, the present week, the date label and the known
sets per audience, and nothing else; a view read, cached per (digest, week, audience) as the tiles are. V15's atlas
reads a member through it alone — never the document, never a raster, never a record — and the picture exports share
its path. It is never a model input and never persisted. **The world scene reads it** (J399 (R3); the table's row
above): the scene's background image is this reading's tiles at the chosen stop for the chosen audience, composed — so
a players' scene is the party's picture as the atlas would show it, with nothing of the DM's in it —, and the scene's
notes are the glyphs and sites that reading draws at the stop; the scene adds a grid the DM chooses (presentation, no
time in it, J399 (R5)) and takes nothing else from the document: no lens, no diagnostic, no wall, no light.

### 5.5 The settlement's picture exports from the world

The base's picture exports are unchanged for a frame; the world's `settlements` layer exports the glyphs as drawn. A
frame's own still may carry the world context strip (its placement's world square at stop 3 as an inset, a dialog
option; own).

### 5.6 Accessibility and the clerk's rendering

Every layer has the base's high-contrast variant (§8.3); the water class overlay carries a pattern as well as a colour
(hatching by class) so it reads without colour; every reason the clerk renders is text (V13 §4.7). The world's
screen-reader summary (V09's) lists the extent, the seas, the named rivers and the settlements by tier.

### 5.7 What the world gives a 2.5D projection (item 141 (e); the renderer is V14's R1–R4 for every document, the world included)

V14's R1–R4 own the 2.5D view of every document, the world document among them (SW-02; J-V13.52); this section
supplies the world's drawables with their `ZDecl` rows (BCR-V13-28; SW-22) and nothing else. The world regime hands
that view exactly these: the fine DEM draped (the vertical exaggeration a view key, never in
any hash — M11); every `WaterSurface` a plane at its `elevationCm` (a lake's, the sea's, a reach's stage profile as a
ruled surface along its course); every trace a plane at its former level (`SurfaceTrace`) or the former ground
(`TerrainTrace`); the glyph marks at the DEM's height at each point; the routes, the seat territory and sway borders, the occupation and debatable hatches, the patrol tints and the event
pins draped on the DEM, and every lens's marks (V13 §5.9) with them; the labels upright at their anchors' heights. **The world's M9 row** (item 140 M9): every world kind declares base
= the DEM and top = the DEM (a raster, a route, a border, a glyph mark, a trace) or its surface (a `WaterSurface`: base
the bed, top the surface); none is flat — as `ZDecl` rows: `{ surface: 'dem' }` for the rasters, routes, borders,
hatches, patrol tints, event pins, lens marks, glyph marks and `TerrainTrace`; `{ base: 'bed', top: 'elevationCm' }` for `WaterSurface` and `SurfaceTrace`; `{ flat,
reason: 'furniture' }` for a label candidate. The projection family, the hit test, the per-stop `Lod25Row`s and the
vertical edit are V14's (R1–R4; V14 §5.6 (10) draws this list); nothing of the world's model changes under any
projection (bar 14's world half: the same document hashes identically under the flat view and every projection —
T-V13-40's row, harnessed on T-V14-14's fixture).

### 5.8 The lens mechanism (J379; J384; one derived layer for every host system the map draws)

A **lens** is a derived layer over the facts the host sends of one of its simulated systems — its plague, its politics
(the sway and patrols lenses, V13 §3.9), its trade, its populations, its faiths, its prosperity and its settlements'
alignment. Every one of those systems keeps its facts per settlement or per pair of settlements: none
is a field over land, links decide who is touched — save four places where nearness picks (a supply link's three
cheapest producers, the column pool's eight nearest, the pilgrim catchment's eight nearest, a satellite's site) — while
geometry otherwise only attenuates, delays or prices, and the host keeps
no history of most of them. So a lens draws marks at settlements, links between them, movers placed by a host clock
and uniform fills over a settlement's own seat area — never a surface interpolated between points — and keeps the
history it scrubs itself. Nothing of a lens is read by a stage, a sway revision, an encounter or the clerk; a lens draws
nothing at random, and sends the host nothing but the DM-placed site offers (V13 §3.11.6).

1. **One record.** Every lens is one `LensLayer` (V13 §2.2), a row of `world.lens` (V13 §2.3) with its element
   functions in `@plat/world/lens`, drawn by one code path: its **identity** (its id, the owner rule that asked for it,
   the host system it draws); its **sources**, each a port field with the **gate expression** that makes it live (a
   host lane lit, the canon, a slot of the host's frozen record, a seated deity, a live plague, belief recorded, the birth defaults, the host's intensity, a field
   sent); its **regime** words ((2)); its **elements**, each with its fact class ((4)), its drawing grammar (glyph, link,
   route flow, moving marker, catchment, area fill, overlay, caption), its gate, the most of the audience it may reach
   ((7)), its scrub source ((8)), its derivation label and its style row; its **events**, the `WorldEvent` kinds it reads
   — one shared store of dated events, each tagged at fold with the lenses it moves by the adapter folder's event table,
   so one occupation, conversion, boom or raid moves every lens it touches at one week and the scrub agrees across
   lenses; its **legend** ((6)); its **refusals** ((4)); and its **why** — `lensWhy` answers per mark with the host facts
   it read and the rule that drew it, the sway's `whyCell` generalised. A lens is added by a row and its element
   functions, never by a second mechanism. Its controls — the lens picker (a row per lens in `world.lens`'s order, a
   still lens collapsed, greyed and openable), the scrub bar with its declared gaps, `pinPlate` and the lens-mark card
   that answers `lensWhy` — behave as this section states; V09 hosts and draws them in the world view (BCR-V13-39) and
   decides none of their rows, gates, answers or audiences. **Its felt row** (J397 (M3); the host's first-visible-latency
   and felt-proof laws carried to the map): every lens names, in `world.lens` (`LensRule.lenses[].felt`) and in a *Felt*
   line under its heading in V13 §5.9, the DM-felt sentence its live regime fires and its first-visible latency in the
   DM's advance unit (week, month, season, year — the unit within which its first mark shows under that regime; its
   still banner shows at the birth window, V13 §5.8 (2)); a lens with no felt row is instrumentation and says so in its
   banner; and, the honesty rule's companion, a lens whose first-visible line fails its experience read does not light —
   it stays a recorded row set, as D-V13.8's are, listed in the picker as still with the reason "not yet proven felt",
   never hidden (T-V13-76).
2. **The regime, before the picture.** The legend's first row is the **regime banner**, computed from the regime the
   host resolves and sends with each lens window (`HostRegime`: whether the campaign runs its birth defaults or an
   applied preset, the canon marker, its frozen record's sea-lane, teleport and seasonal slots, each of its lanes lit or
   dark, a deity seated anywhere, a plague live, belief recorded, its intensity) — never from a preset's name, which over-states what a
   born campaign runs. A lens's regime is the first of its regime words (V13 §5.9) whose gate holds; every regime
   word's gate includes its lens's source sent. A window with no regime raises `W_LENS_REGIME_ABSENT`: every banner reads "the host's regime not sent", and a gated element draws only
   the facts actually sent, labelled "regime unknown" — never a regime guessed from the facts. **At birth** (J397 (M1);
   H37): the host sends the birth window at the campaign's creation — a lens window with its regime resolved and its
   populations, a polity window with its facts at their genesis values (V13 §3.11.6) — so every banner resolves at birth, the sway projects from genesis facts at birth
   and the lens picker never opens on a column of "not sent" for a campaign born on this world; the provisional regime
   of V13 §5.9 (2) narrows to a world bound to an existing campaign before its first polity window, and until H37 lands
   a new campaign opens as that one does; a birth window with no regime is `W_LENS_REGIME_ABSENT` like any other.
3. **The honesty rule** (J384 (13)). An element whose gate is false draws as **still**; a lens whose every gate is false,
   or whose regime is its still word, opens in still mode with its banner and its reason in this volume's words ("no creed crosses a border: the host's
   faith spread is off"; "this band has not moved: the campaign runs no prosperity writer"), listed collapsed in the
   lens picker (greyed, openable) — **never hidden and never extrapolated**: no motion, trend, forecast or spread drawn
   beyond the host's facts. **The built bias said:** where a lens reads biased by the host's own tables — its
   alignment reading's malicious and belligerent lean where the reading rests on archetype, roster and legitimacy only
   (the alignment lens's born regime under any preset, V13 §5.9 (8); never `GateExpr.born`, the birth defaults), its
   prosperity's ratchet (upward in aggregate, a struggling seat sinking) where its festival or boom writer is lit
   (V13 §5.9 (7)), its small seats that cannot grow where its population lane runs (below a head count its intensity
   sets, about a thousand at its conservative intensity; V13 §5.9 (5)) — the legend says it is the host's arithmetic,
   not the realm's history, each note a row of `world.lens` under its own gate (`LensLayer.legend.notes`), shown only
   where that gate holds. **The author said:** at the host's default tuning organic plague is silent, and the host's
   generation seats no deity under any preset, so a lens that shows either shows the DM's authoring, and says so — the
   religion lens's note gated on a deity seated, never on the birth defaults.
4. **No invented fact: four classes of host mark, and only four, beside the DM's own world sites.** (a)
   **host-stored** — a fact the host persists, drawn as stored; (b) **host-derived** — a value the host computes by its
   own law on the same window and sends (in the lens window or on request), labelled "by the host's law": the map never
   calls or re-implements a host law, whose own copies already disagree; (c) **placement** — the map's geometry used
   only to place a host fact (a settlement's seat area, W8a, for a uniform fill; a path laid by `pathGeometry` for a
   link's "likely road"; a frozen site's point), labelled where it is a guess — an element of another class so
   positioned is marked `placed`; (d) **owner-ruled map derivation** — the sway and the patrol cadence the owner's
   territory rules asked for, labelled "projection", never the host's truth: the sway reaches the host only as the map feed's offered readings, which no host reader reads until the host's own ruling admits one (law (10) of V13 §3.11.6; J400 (12)), and the patrol cadence not at all (the host gives it no meaning; J400 (18)). A world site the DM
   placed (V14) is the map's own fact, class `dmPlaced`, labelled "DM-placed". Everything else is **refused** (`refuse.lens.invented`,
   with the refusal's reason): a quantity the host discards (a column's losses on the road, the share of a dispersal it
   loses, a conversion's source it did not send); a field interpolated from point facts; motion without a host clock (a
   caravan between its ends); an effect the host does not apply (a patrol lowering danger, a border stopping a plague,
   migrants carrying a faith); a meaning the host does not compute (a plague as a punishment, a god's region).
5. **Two grammars for movement, and the split between a mover marker and a dated fact** (J397 (M23); the host's
   ambiguity law for movers, amended to say the same, H44). Transfers the host nets within one week draw as **dated
   links** between the two settlements along the host's own links, never along a road; movers the host clocks draw as
   **moving markers** placed by that clock along a placed path; never one grammar for the other. **A mover marker is a
   presence, never an intention:** a column, a named traveller, a shipment or an army on the march draws at its leg's
   fraction of the host's clock and nothing else — no destination drawn, no arrival time on the marker, no path
   highlight, no heading, no purpose; its "likely road" (a `pathGeometry` path, class (4) (c)) is DM-only and labelled,
   and a mover's card names what the host sends and never where it is going. **A dated fact the host computed may
   carry its week on any surface:** an arrival week, an onset week, a hop's week, a departure — the plague's approach
   ring ("word of plague has reached", the weeks to onset), a hop's "arrived week n", a supply arrival, a column's
   arrival once the host's row dates it — each a host-dated row drawn at its seat with its week, public where the host
   so resolves; a column in motion is a mover marker and its arrival a dated fact captioned at the destination only
   once the host's row says it arrived, never a line from the marker to it. A sea link (a sea column, a shipment, a
   plague's crossing) draws along the host's own lane and is placed by the host's own leg time; it reads this volume's
   directional seasonal efforts (V13 §3.8 (12)) only once the host has adopted them (H33) — the map never shows a
   mover faster or slower than the host's clock says —, and until H33 a lens's sea link carries the routes layer's
   seasonal effort for the view's month as a caption beside the host's leg, "the host's movers do not yet read the
   season" (J397 (M27): two seas, both labelled, until one clock serves both); after H33 the caption drops.
6. **The legend's words.** **Host vocabulary as data:** the host's band, phase and chip words travel in the adapter
   folder's vocabulary tables, one per lens, drawn as sent; this volume's own strings are its derivation labels, its
   still reasons and its notes. **One word, one meaning** (`world.lens`'s collision rows, as V13 §3.11.6's law (9) is
   for politics): the host's monster-threat word for a place and its colour are never the plague lens's; *gate* is
   written a border crossing, a route's intermediary settlement or a town gate, never bare; *toll* names which of its
   meanings it is; *besieged* is the war's, never a stressor's; *prosperity* is the host's rung only, never its economic
   capacity or a lifecycle's health; *temperament* is never a legend word; *alignment* is the moral reading, never a
   bloc. **Polarity normalised:** every axis the host sends is turned by the adapter folder's polarity table to one
   convention — lawful high, malicious high, lenient high — the table naming each host axis's own sign.
7. **The audience filter** (J-V13.77's rule for every lens). **The DM by default:** every lens opens DM-only; a row
   the host sends with no resolved audience is folded DM-only; covert links, columns and patrols fail closed — omitted,
   never greyed. **A player** sees only the rows the host resolved public and, where the regime records belief, the
   party's believed rows (`LensFacts` of audience `party`) — **the party's observer** (J397 (M8); H39; J400 (9)): the party's
   believed set is the believed record of the court of the seat where the host's whereabouts of the party
   name ONE seat (`LensFacts.partySeats`: the place the host's party record holds — the DM's present-at in the host,
   else the last heard — sent on its presentation rows), else of the party's home seat (`LensFacts.partyHome`, a field
   of the host's party record the DM sets) — a PAIR (an act between two settlements) reading the home seat's court
   until the host rules a pair's observer, failing closed —, else none — the public truth or nothing —, the host
   resolving the court and naming it (`LensFacts.observer`); the DM's party pin is never read for the observer (it is a
   request the host carries out or the map's own picture, V13 §2.2's `PartyPlacement`) and the map asks no court's
   believed facts for the party's picture, so a rumour that court believes can draw on the party's map and the legend says whose belief
   it is ("as Emberford's court believes it"); every believed row carries its age and confidence band (`Believed`): a
   believed mark draws "as of week n" and fades by band (`LensRule.believed.alphaByBand`), never ageless; the host's
   integrity register word on a believed row or an event (`Believed.integrity`, `WorldEvent.integrity`: clean, worn in
   the telling, planted) is DM-only, dropped from every party set and player picture at fold (J397 (M11)). **Under an
   omniscient regime** the player picture is the public truth or nothing — and, **where the host sends the party's
   whereabouts, the public truth at a rider's pace** (the default-preset arm, J397 (M10); J400 (9)): a public row of a seat at week w
   reaches the party's picture at w + floor(hopWeeks × `partyNewsDelay.factor`), the hop weeks the canon's from the
   row's seat to the NEAREST seat of `LensFacts.partySeats` (its one seat, or the nearer of a pair) under the travel law
   in force (a pair's row from the nearer seat; a realm-wide row from the nearest seat it names; a row of a seat
   `partySeats` names at once; a row with no seat at its week) — the host's
   own distance pricing adopted as data (`LensRule.partyNewsDelay`; `TravelLaw.news` where sent wins) — the DM's
   picture unaffected, the sway's borders moving on the party's map by the same rule (V13 §5.1's player picture) and
   the player legend reading "news reaches the party at a rider's pace"; with no whereabouts sent the delay is not applied
   and the picture is as current as the public truth, and the legend says so; the DM's party pin never measures the
   delay (J400 (9): on a host-bound world the host's whereabouts are the one writer of the party's place), and a
   standalone world has no delay and no observer (there is no host). **The known set grows from the party's places**
   (J399 (R4); J400 (9)): a party's known cells (`RenderedWorld.known`, V13 §2.2; the party key's `places`, V14 §2.3)
   gain the seats of the host's whereabouts from each window's `partyStamp` and the coarse cell of each of the DM's
   map-only party placements from its week — on a standalone world every placement's, the seat's place where a
   placement is at a seat; a present-at placement counts once the host's row carries it, as the host's seats —, never
   a cell between two places: the places are where the party has been, not how it went (the ambiguity law, (5), kept
   for the party itself: the party may teleport, fly or leave the road, so the map never computes its journey); travel
   times stay the routes' labels (V13 §5.1), information and never a journey the map runs — no path, no ETA, no day
   count (T-V13-122; the one writer, T-V13-126; the observer and the delay, T-V13-127). **No player view of alignment** (J384 (7)): the alignment lens refuses every audience but the DM
   (`refuse.lens.audience`), and a party set's alignment rows are dropped at fold; the host's public chips stay where
   the host shows them. **Suppressed creeds and criminal trade DM-only** (J379; J-V13.77's fail-closed rule over the
   host's criminal flags): a party set's suppressed creeds are dropped at fold too, and the host's criminal channels
   and its criminal income never reach a player picture (the income mix is not drawn in this pass).
8. **The time scrub and the plates** (J384 (9)). Every lens draws at the view's `lensWeek` (default the document's week),
   reading, in order: host-dated facts (event weeks; a row's own weeks — an arrival, an onset, a departure, a founding,
   an occupation's start); the sway's revision history (the sway and patrols lenses); **plates** for every fact the host
   keeps no history of (bands, shares, phases, axes, trends); and, before the first plate, the host's own per-advance
   pulse records where it sends them once at first bind (`LensFacts.pulses`: their population deltas and outcome
   severities, at most its 80 advances), labelled with their horizon. A **plate** is written when a lens window folds,
   **one per host advance**: the window's `LensFacts` (both audiences) and its polity facts' seat rungs, delta-coded
   against the previous plate with a whole plate every `plates.keyEvery`, in the world document's plate cache
   (`Document.lensPlates`, BCR-V13-38) —
   outside the model digest, the records digest, the canon and every export's model (V13 §2.7). **The horizon in
   weeks:** full resolution for `plates.fullWeeks` (520) behind the present; older plates compacted to one per
   `plates.compactWeeks` (13), the last plate of each host quarter kept; a plate the DM pins (`pinPlate`, a cache
   command, never an edit) is never compacted, and compaction re-encodes each kept plate against the previous kept plate
   (or whole). A host rewind (a window replace) drops every plate after the rewound window, pinned ones included. Plates
   start at the birth window where the host sends one (J397 (M1); H37: plate 0 at the campaign's creation, so the scrub
   reaches week 0 and the first advance's plate differs from it only where something changed — no week-one artifact; on
   a sequel world (J399 (R1); V13 §2.2's `CampaignRecord`) the next campaign's plate 0 at its `fromWeek`, the earlier
   campaigns' plates standing below it READ-ONLY: a window replace of the live campaign drops no plate below its
   `fromWeek`, a closed campaign's last plate is pinned by its close so compaction never takes it, the plate cache is
   keyed by the world week (a window's `seq` read within its campaign), and the scrub, running back through them, labels
   every week before `fromWeek` "before this campaign: {name}, its year n" and a gap's weeks "between {A} and {B}: n
   years after {A}", drawing nothing live there — the earlier campaign's sways and marks in history alone),
   else at the first advance the map observes, and the scrub declares every gap — before the first plate, beyond what
   the pulse records hold; the interior weeks of a multi-week advance the host did not send; a store the host's quota dropped
   (`W_LENS_PLATE_GAP`) — and replays a decaying quantity only by the host's arithmetic as sent, never by a designed
   curve. **The realm's past** (J400 (21); V13 §2.2's `PastFacts`): where the host sends it, the scrub gains, AHEAD of the
   world clock and claiming none of its weeks, a strip of its own per campaign whose host sent a past, in YEARS ("{n}
   years before the campaign") and never in weeks; on a sequel world each strip is headed "the realm's past, as {name}
   began", counted back from that campaign's first week, its legend adding "the host's history as {name} began — it
   may tell of years when {earlier} was played here", and the strips stand in the campaigns' order, never interleaved
   with any campaign's weeks: a position on a strip draws that year's past facts at their seats and pairs (V13 §5.1's
   `events` row) and nothing else, no plate, sway or lens mark existing there, each fact labelled pencilled until the
   first advance inks it, then inked; a strip is never an earlier campaign's weeks, which the scrub labels "before
   this campaign: {name}, its year n" (law (9) of V13 §3.11.6); with no past sent the scrub begins at week 0 as before.
   A cache: dropping it loses only the scrub's past.
9. **A derived world layer beside the lenses: land cover** (F2; J-V13.116). The cover plate (V13 §3.6 (5)) is NOT a
   lens — a lens is never a field over land and is read by no stage, and land cover is a field — but it shares three
   of this mechanism's rules. Its **audience filter** is (7)'s, under fact class (4) (d) **owner-ruled map derivation**:
   the map's own projection from dated host facts, labelled "derived land cover", reaching the host only as a
   `physicalChange` offer, never its truth; the DM by default; a player sees it only where the host's public facts and
   the party's known places admit the seats it derives from, the cells of an unknown seat's catchment drawn as their
   potential vegetation. Its **scrub** is (8)'s: one cover plate per host advance in the cover cache beside the lens
   plates (`Document.coverPlates`, BCR-V13-41), a disturbance's plate at its week, read at `lensWeek`, the same horizon
   and compaction — and, unlike a lens plate, re-derivable: a dropped cache rebuilds, since the plate is a pure
   function. **The birth fold** (J397 (M1)): the first cover plate folds at the campaign's creation from the populations
   `CampaignFacts` carries (`SettlementFacts.population`; the birth window's `sizes` where the host sends both, the
   window's winning), so a campaign born on this world is born with its fields, and the first advance's plate differs
   from it only where a dated fact moved the use — never a burst of fields at week one; a campaign with neither reads
   the tier medians below. **A sequel's baseline** (J399 (R1); T-V13-121): the binding of the next campaign
   (`bindCampaign`, V13 §3.11.6) is a dated fact and folds a plate at the new campaign's `fromWeek` — the earlier
   campaign's last plate carried forward by the fold's own law over the dated series: the seats the new campaign does
   not re-bind withdrawn from the earlier campaign's `toWeek` (the close is their withdrawal week, so their fields enter
   the biome's succession over the gap), its re-bound seats held at its last demand, every disturbance recovering over
   the gap's weeks (`gapWeeks` of campaign time and nothing geological: no raster, landform or surface moves at a
   binding) —, and that plate is the new campaign's BASELINE until its first fold, the birth fold above at its birth
   window, which re-reads the use from its own populations; no fold reads a plate's classes (T-V13-62): the baseline is a
   fold over the dated series — the earlier campaign's windows and demand counts, its events and disturbances, the
   close and the binding — as every plate is, and the earlier campaign's this-happened disturbances stand as ground:
   they shaped it, and the ground they shaped is what the new campaign is born on. Its **honesty rule** is (3)'s: a window with no seat populations draws the tier medians and says so in the
   legend; a campaign with no host draws the potential vegetation alone, labelled. Its legend's first row names it the
   map's own derivation, never a host fact: "the fields, pastures and regrowth the map derives from the campaign's
   dated facts; the host's dossier holds the biome". It is registered in the view's layer registry as `landCover` (V13
   §5.1): its overlay form draws in the default picture under `relief` (J394), its thematic form under `worldLayer:
   'landCover'`, never under `worldLens`; nothing of it is read by a stage, a sway revision, an
   encounter's generation or the clerk's placement proposal (T-V13-62's lint).
10. **The view reading** (`viewFacts(world, week, audience)` → `ViewFacts`, V13 §2.2; the spine's §14 (4); file r item
   1012; J-V13.133). The relational style (V15 §3.6) reads a world's host facts through ONE reading: the religion lens's
   hierarchy, faith places, patrons, contested seats and realm rank ((6)'s rows of V13 §5.9), the sway's allegiances with
   their roots and members, each seat's tier, size third and prosperity rung with the realm's held median, the relations
   with their `atWar` and the culture bands ((2), (5) and (7)'s rows; V13 §3.9), the trade lens's entrepôt centrality,
   exports and channels ((4)'s rows), the dated events of the kinds the caller names with their resolved audience (V13
   §2.2's `WorldEvent`), every route in force at `week` with its polyline, stations and sailing (`ViewFacts.routes`, both modes) and the law's storm factors — each from the plates at `week` ((8)'s scrub,
   never later than the present) and the event index, filtered by audience as (7) filters a lens: the DM everything; a
   party or the public only the rows the host resolved so, a DM-only row never returned; never the alignment lens (J384
   (7)), a suppressed creed, a covert link or a criminal channel. What the host never sent is returned as absent by field
   name, never a default, so the reader's legend says so ((3)'s honesty rule). It is fact class (4) at its reader — an
   owner-ruled projection, labelled "projection" — and a view read, never persisted and read by no stage; it is the only
   reading of a world the relational style takes beside `renderAt` (T-V13-68 (j)).

### 5.9 The lenses (J384 (8)'s order; each a row set of V13 §5.8's mechanism)

Each lens below gives its regime words (the first whose gate holds names the regime; the last is its still word), its
elements — *class* **S** host-stored, **D** host-derived, **P** placement, **M** owner-ruled map derivation,
**DM-placed** the DM's own world site; *placed* marks a host fact positioned by map geometry, labelled —, their
audience and scrub, and its refusals — with, under them, the host facts it does not draw in this pass and why, so an
omission is never silent. Every element reads the port's fields (V13 §2.2); every host word comes from the
adapter folder's table for the lens. Three further lenses — culture, danger and calamity — are recorded, not built:
each a later row set of this mechanism, outside J384 (8)'s eight (D-V13.8).

**1. Plague** (J381; the proving lens, first). *Regimes:* **front** (the canon marker set and a plague live: the
host's front walks hop by hop along its trade and shipment links, each hop at its own travel time; on the canon the
host still spreads it within the same week along its migration and service links, drawn as footprint marks beside the
front), **footprint** (a plague live without the canon and the host's same-week spread lit: the host spreads it within
the same week along its links, with no source and no time), **still** (no plague live; or, without the canon, the
host's same-week spread dark: "nothing moves between settlements"). *Notes:* the authorship note of V13 §5.8 (3); "a
border, a march, a patrol or an army neither stops nor slows it: the host's plague reads none of them"; the lens's hue
and words never the monster-threat chip's. *Felt:* "word of plague has reached Kessar: three weeks to onset" — first
visible within one week of an authored outbreak (the approach ring and the hop's arrival); its still banner at the
birth window (J397 (M3)).

| element | reads | drawn | class | regime | audience | scrub |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| phase | `LensFacts.plague[].phase`, `.band` (the host's epidemic ledger, kept on the canon only) | a glyph at the seat in the host's phase words (approaching, active, receding), banded on the host's own edges | S | front | the host's banded fiction public where it so resolves; the truth DM | plate |
| stage | a footprint row's `.stage` and `.severity` as sent | a glyph by the host's stage word, no phase word | S | footprint; front (its same-week joins) | per row | plate |

| approach | `.onsetWeek` | a ring at the seat with the weeks to onset ("word of plague has reached") — a dated fact the host computed, never a mover's intention, so its weeks show on every surface (V13 §5.8 (5); J397 (M23)) | S | front | public where the host so resolves | host-dated |

*Refusals:* a field, gradient or region of disease; an arrow or a time on a footprint; a phase word on a footprint row;
a carrier the host did not send; deaths or losses estimated; a quarantine line; a border, march, patrol, army or
migrant drawn carrying or stopping it; a divine meaning; a merge with the calamity marks; the monster-threat word or
colour. *Not drawn in this pass:* the town's plague condition (a town-map row: the settlement frame draws it among the
dossier conditions it draws, V13 §2.2's knowledge paragraph; a plague arriving through the stressor alone shows
nothing there until H24 closes that gap).

**2. Sway** (the owner's territory: J377, J378, J382; V13 §3.9; second, with patrols). Its layers are V13 §5.1's
`seatTerritory`, `sway`, `occupation`, `debatable` and `fighting`; its scrub is the sway's revision history.
*Regimes:* **enforced** (a polity window carrying force bands: held by force drawn), **civil** (a polity window
without them: held by force only by a host fight verdict's hold band, V13 §3.9 (11) (J386), every other debatable cell
staying debatable, and the legend says the host's military reading is
not yet sent), **provisional** (a host-bound world bound to an existing campaign before its first polity window — a
campaign born on this world receives its polity facts at their genesis values with the birth window's polity half, H37, and opens
provisional only until H37 lands, J397 (M1): each seat projects at its tier with
the middle rung, V13 §3.9's edges, labelled "before the host's first polity window"), **recipe** (a standalone world:
the recipe's seats, links and relations, V13 §3.9 (5)), **still** (no seed: nothing to project). Two banner notes per
window: "the push between adversaries is the host's strength order" or "level: the host's strength order not sent";
"water carries the sway along the host's lanes" or "water bars the sway: the host's lanes are dark". **The label**
(J400 (2), withdrawing J397 (M22)'s host name): an allegiance's legend label reads the DM's christening — a name the
host's realm past offers only once the DM confirms it —, else the descriptive label from its root's name (V13 §3.9
(17)); the host mints no polity name.
**The court viewpoint** (J397 (M9); H40) — HELD by the host (J400 (10)): its projection carries the DM's truth and the party's believed rows and never a court's view, so `LensFacts.courts` stays absent until the host's information program rules a court's view; meanwhile no host-bound world offers this viewpoint, and the court audience of `renderAt` and `viewFacts` and V15's court viewpoint draw their degraded arm, the public record within the court's reach —: where the host sends a court's believed political facts (`LensFacts.courts`:
believed allegiance labels and strength bands, each with its age and confidence), the sway lens offers, per court the
host sent, a viewpoint (`CourtViewpoint`, §2.4) — W8b's rule function run over that court's believed facts in place of the window's: the
believed allegiance label as each subject's member link, the believed strength band as the push, every other input
(tier, size third, prosperity rung, the relations' classes, the water lanes) the host's public facts at that plate and
never a DM-only or covert fact, a subject the court holds no belief of left unclaimed and labelled "unknown to
{court}" — computed on demand as a derived transient (never a `SwayRevision`, never persisted, never in the map feed: law (3) of V13 §3.11.6), cached per (plate, court) and evicted with the plate, its projection within `WORLD-23` (V13 §6), scrubbed by plates, captioned "as {court} believes
it, as of week n" (n the newest `asOfWeek` among the rows read, the oldest named beside it) and drawn with the
believed rows' fade; **DM-only unless the DM opens it** to the party (the lens picker's open switch for that court, a
view key V09 draws under BCR-V13-39, never an edit), and opened it shows the party exactly the court's rows filtered to
the party's audience, never a truth the court does not hold; the party's map uses the party observer's court's
viewpoint where the host sends that court's facts, else the known truth (V13 §5.1's player picture); `whyCell` under a
viewpoint answers with the believed rows it read and their ages, never the truth. *Felt:* "the border moved at
Thornhold's ford: the host's strength order changed" — first visible within one week as the planting line of V13 §3.9
(13), the border itself at its dwell; under a viewpoint, "as Thornhold's court believes it, the ford is still theirs"
(J397 (M3)).

**3. Patrols** (J378; second, with the sway). Its layer is V13 §5.1's `patrols`. *Regimes:* **watched** (the host's

§3.11.6), read from the dated facts its windows carry (V13 §8.5's H9, H13, H23, H25) and drawn as such, never as a

## 6 Performance budgets (§12's form)

**Reference hardware and method** are §12.1's; the measure is the generation worker's wall clock at p95 over five seeds
per rung, nightly, with the work-limit laws of V13 §3.17 as the fitted measures (§13.2's cost-model test: log-log slope
≤ 1.15 for the raster stages (linear in cells) and ≤ 1.25 for W4, W7 and W8 (n log n in the queue)).

**The world's one-click path** (a `generate` with a `WorldRecipe`; the budgets are the size rows' `budgetMs`):

| stage | work measure | province (1.02 M fine, 16 k coarse) | realm (4.1 M / 64 k) | continent (9.2 M / 144 k) | law (p95) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W0 | ops; the planned sites | 1 ms (+ 10 with an included campaign) | 1 ms (+ 15) | 2 ms (+ 20) | ≤ 2 ms + 2 ms × included settlements |
| the formation op (at its bake only, inside W1's first run; `formationMs`) | formation cells × the fixed point's passes | 270 ms | 1 000 ms | 2 300 ms | ≤ `formationMs` (400 / 1 300 / 2 800): the blocks ≈ 100 ns × formation cells, the fixed point ≈ 1 500 ns × formation cells (10 iterations × tree + integral), the talus ≈ 500 ns, the glacial ≈ 300 ns, the second stand ≈ 1 500 ns, the soils ≈ 10 ns × formation cells — never on a later run (the bake is read) |
| W1 | Σ (op cost × touched cells), the costs V13 §2.3's (`continent` template: one 6-octave `noise` = 12 units, two `range` = 4, three `hill` = 3, one `smooth` of one pass = 3, one `mask` = 1 — 23 units over the extent; C13-10) | 350 ms | 1 400 ms | 3 170 ms | ≤ 15 ns × Σ (op cost × touched cells) |
| W2 | fine cells | 25 ms | 100 ms | 230 ms | ≤ 25 ns × cells |
| W3 | 12 months × passes × coarse cells; the basin solves | 75 ms | 300 ms | 680 ms | ≤ 12 × 30 ns × 8 × coarse cells + 12 × `currents.cycles` × 30 ns × the basins' cells (the march 46 / 180 / 420 ms; the currents 29 / 120 / 260 ms at half ocean) |
| W4 | fine cells × log | 180 ms | 760 ms | 1 800 ms | ≤ 10 ns × 12 × cells × (1 + log₂ cells ÷ 24) |
| W5 | fine cells (the classification over the 24 monthly values sampled, the overrides) | 60 ms | 250 ms | 560 ms | ≤ 60 ns × cells (the matrix path 20 ns × cells as before) |
| W6a + W6b | fine cells + candidates × retries | 30 ms | 120 ms | 270 ms | ≤ 25 ns × cells + 2 µs × candidates |
